articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski reveals how two losses helped him become “dad and Alex” again
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski says suffering two losses helped him reconnect with life outside fighting.
articles.body: Alexander Volkanovski says suffering two losses helped him reconnect with life outside fighting. The UFC featherweight champion revealed that he stepped back from putting his career first and focused more on being himself and spending time with his family.Volkanovski said the change allowed him to return to the identity of “Dad and Alex” after nearly 15 years of structuring his life around training. He believes the experience helped him grow and find a better balance between his family life and his demanding career.Alexander Volkanovski found balance after two lossesAlexander Volkanovski opened up about the change after going through a difficult period in his career. The Australian suffered back-to-back defeats before taking time to reset and look at life away from the Octagon.Rather than describing the period as working on himself, Volkanovski said it was more about becoming himself again. He explained how his daily routine changed after years of putting training and competition at the centre of his life.“I obviously had the two losses. I wouldn’t say work on myself, just be myself again. I was Dad and Alex, and the training schedule worked around that for the first time in like 15 years. And it was incredible. I grew so much, and now I find this perfect balance, which is good”, he said.The change appears to have given Volkanovski a different perspective on his career. For years, his schedule was built around preparing for fights. Training, recovery and competition often dictated how he spent his time.After the losses, that approach changed. His family became a bigger part of his daily routine, while training had to fit around his responsibilities as a father.Volkanovski has spent much of his professional career competing at the highest level. He became UFC featherweight champion in 2019 after defeating Max Holloway. He then defended the title multiple times. He established himself as one of the leading fighters in the division.His unbeaten run at featherweight eventually came to an end against Ilia Topuria in 2024. He later suffered another defeat before returning to the win column. He reclaimed the featherweight championship against Diego Lopes.Now, Volkanovski is preparing for another major test. He is scheduled to defend his featherweight title against undefeated contender Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on October 24, 2026, in Abu Dhabi.However, Volkanovski enters this stage of his career with a different outlook. His recent comments suggest that fighting no longer has to define every part of his life.The 38-year-old has previously spoken about the intense demands of fight preparation. articles.title: Muere el ‘Tyson Ruso’ a los 40 años tras una carrera truncada por un misterioso accidente en el metro de Berlín
articles.standfirst: El prometedor Denis Boytsov apareció gravemente herido en una vía de metro en 2015 y perdió la capacidad de andar y hablar
articles.summary: El prometedor Denis Boytsov apareció gravemente herido en una vía de metro en 2015 y perdió la capacidad de andar y hablar
articles.body: El mundo del boxeo está de luto tras conocerse el fallecido del exboxeador ruso Denis Boytsov a los 40 años. La causa de la muerte, según informó el centro deportivo regional de Oriol (Rusia), su ciudad natal, fue un coágulo de sangre, si bien Boytsov llevaba 11 años incapacitado. El ruso, que desarrolló toda su carrera en Alemania, fue considerado en su momento uno de los mayores talentos mundiales del peso pesado. En su mejor momento, Boytsov se convirtió en un potencial aspirante al título mundial de Wladimir Klitschko, pero su carrera terminó tras un grave accidente en Berlín en 2015, cuyas circunstancias nunca quedaron claras. Con un récord de 36-1 (27 KOs), el púgil obtuvo el apodo del ‘Tyson ruso’ debido a su potente golpeo (ganó por KO 18 de sus primeras 20 peleas), a su forma de boxear y a que físicamente era de un corte similar al de ‘Iron Mike’. Llegó a ser campeón Intercontinental de la WBA y segundo clasificado de las listas de este organismo, por lo que se le propuso como aspirante al título de Klitschko. En aquellos años de ascenso llegó a barajarse también un combate contra el emergente Tyson Fury. En realidad, estuvo a una pelea de luchar por el título mundial, pero en noviembre de 2013 Boytsov perdió contra Alex Leapai (decisión unánime con dos derribos) en una eliminatoria mundialista y ahí retrocedió varias casillas. Hizo tres combates posteriormente que poco a poco lo encaminaron de nuevo hacia su propósito, pero entonces sufrió un extraño accidente. En 2015, Boytsov fue encontrado inconsciente y gravemente herido en las vías de un túnel del metro de Berlín, entre dos estaciones. Su apartamento estaba a tan solo unos cientos de metros. El joven, que entonces tenía 29 años, fue trasladado de urgencia al hospital con graves lesiones en la cabeza y las manos. Allí fue sometido a una intervención de emergencia y posteriormente se le indujo un coma. Aquello dejó a Denis incapacitado para caminar y hablar. Las graves consecuencias de sus lesiones marcaron su vida desde ese momento. Aún no está claro cómo llegó al túnel del metro. La esposa de Boytsov, Olga, temió que su marido hubiera sido víctima de una venganza, pero tras analizar las declaraciones de los testigos y las grabaciones de vídeo, la policía de Berlín consideró que se trató de un accidente. No hubo pruebas de la participación de terceros en este incidente y la policía concluyó que Boytsov había sufrido sus lesiones de forma accidental mientras se encontraba en estado de embriaguez. Boytsov pasó siete semanas en coma inducido médicamente antes de comenzar su recuperación, si bien las secuelas neurológicas fueron muy graves. Se sometió a años de rehabilitación en Alemania antes de regresar a Rusia.

articles.title: Dana White Dismisses Rumors of UFC Saudi Arabia Event Being Rescheduled Amid Tensions in the Middle East
articles.summary: Dana White has confirmed that the UFC's event schedule is set to go as planned despite attacks and regional violence in Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
Growing security concerns in the Middle East have cast doubt over several major combat sports events scheduled in the region. Recent missile and drone attacks targeting critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, have raised questions about whether upcoming sporting events can proceed as planned.

According to DW News, Ansar Allah, the Yemeni movement commonly known as the Houthis, has repeatedly targeted Riyadh airport . The report cited an October 10 attack that killed 12 people and injured around 300, adding to concerns about security in the region.

The uncertainty has also put the UFC's rumored December 5 Fight Night in the spotlight. The card is expected to feature Israel Adesanya against Shara Magomedov, but speculation has emerged that the event could be canceled or moved elsewhere. Dana White , however, has offered a different outlook, suggesting the UFC is still moving ahead with its plans for the Middle East.

Dana White Says UFC Has No Plans to Alter Its Upcoming Fight Schedule

The December 5 card is not the only UFC event attracting attention amid the regional tensions. UFC 333 is scheduled for October 24 in Abu Dhabi, where Alexander Volkanovski is set to defend his featherweight title against Movsar Evloev.

Boxing has also been caught up in the uncertainty. Canelo Alvarez's planned October 31, 2026, fight against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh could face complications, with prominent boxing figures, including WBC champion Sebastian Fundora, voicing concerns about security following the airport attacks.

Meanwhile, tennis has already seen a major change to its schedule. The Six Kings Slam, originally planned for late October, has reportedly been postponed until December. Despite the uncertainty surrounding other sporting events, White has indicated that the UFC has no immediate plans to change its Middle East schedule.

Speaking at the UFC Edmonton post-fight press conference , the UFC CEO outlined his busy travel schedule and upcoming events in the region. He said, "I go to Abu Dhabi on Tuesday; I have like six events in the next 30 days in Saudi, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi."

White's comments came after Russian outlet Vestnik MMA reported that the December 5 Riyadh event could be scrapped altogether. According to the report, the rumored middleweight clash between Adesanya and Magomedov could instead move to UFC Qatar, scheduled for November 21.

The situation has also sparked debate about how UFC leadership handles staff safety when events are scheduled in areas facing security concerns. Ant Evans recently shared an account on X about the approach taken before UFC 120 in London back in October 2010.

According to Evans, Zuffa's head of security sent a company-wide email warning that London was extremely dangerous and advising staff to remain in their hotel at night. He also claimed that Las Vegas had recorded more violent crime that year than the entire United Kingdom.

Although the warning may have seemed excessive to some, Evans argued that it showed the company was taking employee safety seriously. He contrasted that approach with the current situation, raising concerns about TKO and the UFC sending staff into a region experiencing serious security tensions.

Ultimately, White's comments suggest that the promotion intends to stick to its current schedule for now.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois vs Moses Itauma is an all-British heavyweight rivalry for the future | 'British boxing's in a great position'
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois scored a stunning two-round victory in Saturday's rematch with Fabio Wardley to defend the WBO heavyweight world title; Moses Itauma has to rebuild from his IBF world championship defeat to Filip Hrgovic but can return to set himself on a collision course with Dubois
articles.body:
The sport in the UK has been dominated by the personalities and talents of Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury over the last decade. Although Fury and Joshua didn't box each other when they were both reigning world champions, they will finally fight in December in Cardiff.

That really will be a swansong bout for Fury and Joshua. While it's hard to imagine Dubois and Itauma matching the levels of fame Fury and AJ enjoyed, they can emulate them as two British rivals taking over the top of the heavyweight division.

They can also differ from Fury and AJ in a crucial regard - they don't have to leave actually fighting each other until the autumn of their careers. Both Dubois and Itauma are young, especially for heavyweights. Dubois is 29 years old and Itauma just 21.

They can fight in their primes, and they've got the time to box twice, even three times, in their careers if merited.

Dubois is riding high now. His two defeats to Oleksandr Usyk feel long distant after Dubois won an epic brawl in a first fight with Fabio Wardley to claim the WBO world title and most recently demolished Wardley in a rematch to defend the belt.

Itauma has to come back from defeat to Filip Hrgovic, a first professional loss for the fast-rising star.

Fighting for the IBF world title, Itauma outboxed Hrgovic, only to suddenly tire and unravel. Hrgovic, after absorbing punishment for eight rounds, stopped Itauma in the ninth.

Itauma now finds himself with questions to answer and a point to prove, just as Dubois did in his first career defeat when he took a knee against Joe Joyce in 2020.

Dubois is backing Itauma to come back and return to the heavyweight title picture.

"I hope so," Dubois said. "You need dance partners."

Frank Warren promotes both Dubois and Itauma. He believes Itauma will be improved by the defeat. "That's what makes you a better fighter," Warren said.

"He's 21 years of age. He'll have a comeback fight [in January] and I'm sure he'll come through it and then we'll look at all the various scenarios. But he'll want to be involved in it.

"What a great position that British boxing's in," Warren added. "This is not something that just happened overnight, we worked hard for this.

"We are on a mission to get these heavyweights under an umbrella but make the fights happen."

articles.title: Smith vs Puello: Date, ringwalk, UK time, undercard, weight, venue, records & how to follow
articles.summary: All you need to know about WBC light-welterweight champion Dalton Smith's defence against Alberto Puello in Sheffield on Saturday.
articles.body:
Dalton Smith makes the first defence of his WBC light-welterweight world title against former champion Alberto Puello in Sheffield on Saturday, 24 October.

The unbeaten Smith, 29, returns to his home city nine months after producing the biggest victory of his career by stopping Subriel Matias in New York to become world champion.

It is a homecoming which has been a long time coming.

Smith was originally due to face mandatory challenger Puello at the Utilita Arena in June, only for an injury suffered in training to force the fight to be postponed .

Dominican Puello, 32, is a former WBA and WBC champion whose only professional defeat came against Matias.

Can Smith cap his breakthrough year with another statement win? Or can Puello regain the title he lost in 2025?

All you need to know about the fight night is below.

Champion Smith dreams of Hillsborough after homecoming

Live text commentary will begin at 21:00 BST on Saturday, 24 October on the BBC Sport website and app.

Radio commentary from London will begin at 22:00 on BBC Radio 5 Live.

Stacey Copeland will present the live coverage, joined by lead commentator Ronald McIntosh, with Steve Bunce and former super-middleweight world champion Richie Woodhall providing co-commentary.

What time are the ringwalks for Smith v Puello?

Smith and Puello are expected to make their ringwalks at about 22:00 BST , although the exact time will depend on the length of the undercard.

The main broadcast is scheduled to begin at about 19:00 , with doors at the Utilita Arena opening at 16:00 .

Smith v Puello undercard & running order

Dalton Smith v Alberto Puello - WBC light-welterweight title

Giorgio Visioli v Maxi Hughes - vacant WBC International Silver lightweight title

Shannon Ryan v Emma Dolan - British, Commonwealth and IBF Inter-Continental super-flyweight titles

Edward Hardy v Ibrahim Nadim - super-featherweight

Aqib Fiaz v Jordan Flynn - super-featherweight

Joe Hayden v Will Harrison - welterweight

Connor Mitchell v TBA - super-featherweight

Chris Mulunda v Harley Collison - middleweight

Smith won English, British, Commonwealth and European honours on his way through the domestic ranks.

He travelled to Brooklyn in January as the challenger against one of the division's most feared punchers.

Matias had won 22 of his 23 professional victories by stoppage and Smith was fighting in the United States for the first time.

The Sheffield fighter elected to trade with Matias and, in a thrilling fifth round, dropped the Puerto Rican with a huge right hand before the referee stopped the contest.

It was the first time Matias had been stopped as a professional and took Smith's unbeaten record to 19 victories, with 14 inside the distance.

How tough a homecoming is this for Smith?

Smith enters with a perfect record of 19 wins from 19 fights, with 14 knockouts.

There are easier opponents to choose for a first world-title defence but Smith does not have a choice as Puello is his mandatory challenger.

The Dominican has 25 wins from 26 professional fights, with 11 knockouts, and has already twice held a version of a world title.

Puello won the WBA belt by beating Batyr Akhmedov in 2022 and later defeated the highly rated Gary Antuanne Russell to claim the WBC interim title.

He was elevated to full champion and went on to beat Sandor Martin before losing the belt to Matias by majority decision in July 2025.

Puello also presents Smith with a very different stylistic challenge to Matias. Rather than applying relentless pressure, he is a slick southpaw who relies on movement, speed and counter-punching.

Smith has long been regarded as one of British boxing's leading prospects, but victory over Matias moved him onto the world stage and a successful first defence would strengthen his claim to be one of the best fighters in the division.

It could also open the door to much bigger fights. Shakur Stevenson holds the WBO title, while Russell is the WBA champion. The IBF title is vacant.

There is also a domestic rivalry developing with unbeaten Londoner Adam Azim.

Azim is 15-0 and has been talked about as a future world champion, but Smith has, for now, moved ahead of him in terms of achievement by winning a recognised world title.

Should Azim reach that level, a future all-British world-title fight could become one of the biggest contests available to both men.

Promoter Eddie Hearn has previously talked about the prospect of Smith eventually headlining at Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough Stadium if his profile continues to grow, while Smith has spoken about wanting to build the kind of travelling support Ricky Hatton enjoyed at his peak.

Beating a former champion of Puello's quality on home soil would help show whether he can become one of British boxing's headline names.

articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski has revealed the brutal challenge his team puts newcomers through during fight week.

The Australian UFC featherweight champion admitted that the intense test has previously left participants vomiting and suffering pulled hamstrings.The challenge has attracted attention as Volkanovski prepares to defend his featherweight title against undefeated contender Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on October 24, 2026, in Abu Dhabi. articles.title: Dricus du Plessis targets UFC middleweight title return before making bold light heavyweight championship claim
articles.summary: Dricus du Plessis has revealed his plans to reclaim the UFC middleweight championship before moving up to light heavyweight.
articles.body: Dricus du Plessis has revealed his plans to reclaim the UFC middleweight championship before moving up to light heavyweight. The former champion believes he has what it takes to become a titleholder in the 205-pound division as well.Du Plessis wants to return to the top at 185 pounds first. However, he is already looking beyond middleweight and is confident that his size and skills will help him succeed against bigger opponents.Dricus du Plessis eyes middleweight comeback before light heavyweight moveDricusDu Plessis has made his intentions clear as he looks to rebuild his position in the UFC. The South African lost his middleweight championship to Khamzat Chimaev at UFC 319 in August 2025. Chimaev secured a unanimous decision victory to take the title away from the former champion.“I want to get my belt back and eventually go up to 205 and go test myself there. And I’m certain that I’ll be a champion. I’m big enough for that division, and I’m certain I can be champion at that division as well”, he said.The defeat ended Du Plessis’ reign at the top of the 185-pound division. However, he has continued to pursue his goal of becoming champion again.The South African returned to winning ways in July 2026. He defeated former UFC welterweight champion Kamaru Usman by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 281. The victory gave Du Plessis an important result as he continued his journey back towards the middleweight title picture.Despite his ambitions at light heavyweight, Du Plessis does not want to rush into a new division. His immediate priority remains reclaiming the belt at 185 pounds. He wants to establish himself as the best middleweight again before testing his abilities against larger opponents.A move to light heavyweight would present a different challenge. Fighters in the division compete at a maximum weight limit of 205 pounds. The additional size and strength could make the transition difficult, but Du Plessis believes he has the physical attributes required to compete at that level.His confidence also suggests that he would not move up simply to experience another weight class. He wants to compete for the championship and prove that he can succeed against elite opponents in a second division.Du Plessis previously established himself as one of the leading fighters at 185 pounds before losing his title to Chimaev. Reclaiming the championship would be an important step towards fulfilling his longer-term ambitions.His plan is straightforward. He wants to regain the middleweight belt, prove himself at the top of the division and then move up to 205 pounds.Du Plessis is confident that his size and abilities will allow him to become a light heavyweight champion too. articles.title: El morbo del Policía vs. Exconvicto de bare-knuckle termina en un KO brutal
articles.standfirst: El ex de UFC Jimmie Rivera dio cuenta de Brandon Meyer con una acción rápida y limpia
articles.summary: El ex de UFC Jimmie Rivera dio cuenta de Brandon Meyer con una acción rápida y limpia
articles.body: Jimmie Rivera, exluchador de UFC y Bellator, no ha competido en MMA desde 2021, tras su derrota ante Pedro Munhoz en UFC Fight Night 186. Desde entonces, ‘El Terror’ se ha centrado en el combate a puño descubierto y actualmente tiene un récord de 4-2-1 en Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC). El sábado por la noche, Rivera regresó a BKFC para enfrentarse a Brandon Meyer en el evento coestelar de BKFC 95 en Newark. Esta fue la séptima pelea de Rivera en el ring de dicha compañía y no le va mal. El luchador de Nueva Jersey logró su primera victoria por KO en esta promoción el pasado octubre, pero en su última aparición se superó, propinando un brutal KO de un solo golpe en el cuarto asalto. La contienda venía precedida de cierto morbo, ya que Rivera es policía a tiempo completo y BKFC lo programó contra Brandon Meyer, un luchador que pasó 12 años en prisión. Rivera incluso bromeó antes diciendo que Meyer podría darle una paliza sin ser arrestado. Pero las cosas no salieron exactamente así, ya que en el cuarto asalto Rivera acorraló a Meyer contra las cuerdas y le propinó un gancho de izquierda perfecto que lo envió a la lona. En bare-knuckle este tipo de noqueos están a la orden del día, pero sin duda la acción de Rivera fue muy limpia, al igual que la de Cole Cameron esa misma noche.

articles.title: Merab Dvalishvili: "Quiero romperle la cara a Petr Yan"
articles.standfirst: El peleador georgiano ha calentado la trilogía con el campeón de peso gallo antes del UFC 333 de este sábado
articles.summary: El peleador georgiano ha calentado la trilogía con el campeón de peso gallo antes del UFC 333 de este sábado
articles.body: Este sábado Abu Dhabi acogerá uno de los mayores eventos del año: el UFC 333. En esta cartelera habrá dos combates titulares, y uno de ellos será la trilogía entre Merab Dvalishvili (21-5) y Petr Yan (20-5) por el cinturón de peso gallo. Antes del gran día, el peleador georgiano ha dado una entrevista con Stake y ha mostrado las ganas que tiene de vengarse del peleador ruso después de perder el cinturón contra él en diciembre de 2025 y ver cómo se acababa una racha histórica. El año pasado, Dvalishvili fue el campeón más activo de la UFC, realizando hasta cuatro defensas de cinturón y consagrándose posiblemente como el GOAT de la categoría. Tras convertirse en campeón en septiembre de 2024, 'The Machine' logró defender el título ante Umar Nurmagomedov, Sean O'Malley y Cory Sandhagen. Sin embargo, Merab pecó de exceso de actividad y en su cuarta defensa Yan igualó su rivalidad tras pasarle por encima y evitar una gesta sin precedentes. Después de este tropiezo, Merab pasó de pelear cuatro veces en 2025 a tomarse casi un año de descanso, el cuál llegará a su fin este sábado para intentar recuperar el título. "Quiero simplificar las cosas. Quiero romperle la cara e intentar noquearlo. La última vez no salió como esperaba, pero creo que esta vez sí lo conseguiré", sentenció 'The Machine' en la entrevista con Stake. Además, añadió que "pelear contra Petr Yan es difícil, pero me he preparado muy bien y he entrenado muchísimo. Ya me he enfrentado a él dos veces, pero esta es una pelea diferente. Ahora mismo es el mejor del mundo y me estoy preparando a conciencia. Por si fuera poco, si Merab consigue cerrar la trilogía con éxito tiene claro a quién quiere enfrentar en la primera defensa de su segundo reinado. "Me gustaría enfrentarme a Song Yadong. Nunca hemos peleado entre nosotros y creo que es el siguiente rival más fuerte. Todos sabemos que tiene poder de K.O. Sería un gran combate, arriesgado y exigente, pero estoy preparado". En cuanto al descanso tan largo que ha tenido, Dvalishvili ha desvelado que no estaba en sus planes, ya que su intención era volver mucho antes. "Estaba preparado para volver a pelear en marzo. Tenía esperanzas de hacerlo porque sabía que nos habían dicho que nuestro combate no sería en la Casa Blanca en junio y que pelearía antes de esa fecha. ¿Necesitaba descansar? No, pero he disfrutado de este tiempo y creo que me ha venido bien porque he tenido más margen para entender lo que tengo que hacer en mi próximo combate contra Yan", finalizó. La espera ya ha terminado, y este sábado se saldará de una vez por todas una rivalidad que puede definir al GOAT de la categoría. El mejor grappler contra el mejor striker en un choque de estilos que tiene todos los alicientes para ser uno de los mejores combates del año.

articles.title: Cheavon Clarke vs Chris Billam-Smith: 'C4' set for all-British cruiserweight bout at Copper Box Arena
articles.summary: Cheavon Clarke and Chris Billam-Smith resume their rivalry in the professional ranks as the main event on Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on November 7, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Billam-Smith lost to Clarke in the final of the national elite amateur championships in 2016, a result which the Bournemouth fighter believes denied him a place in the Team GB boxing squad.

The British cruiserweight duo will resume their rivalry in the professional ranks as the main event on Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on November 7, live on Sky Sports .

But Clarke, who also defeated Billam-Smith in an English title belt series, told Sky Sports : "I beat him twice [as an amateur], but I haven't got any hook-ups on it.

"Maybe he has. We're professionals now and it's a new era."

Clarke went on to represent Team GB at the Tokyo Olympics, while Billam-Smith secured his ultimate achievement as a professional when he had a spell as the WBO world champion.

But the 36-year-old has admitted he is still irritated by his defeat a decade ago to Clarke.

Watching back footage, Billam-Smith said: "At the time I thought I had done enough to win it, but he's the aggressor, he hit me with some good shots.

"What I will say is the style there is a lot different to my style now. I look so frail and upright. It's very different to how I box now, but it was great, it was a great learning curve for me.

"But that was very much the beginning of the end of my amateur career. Obviously I had GB assessments off the back of it, but he got on and I didn't after he beat me. They were going to choose him on the GB team.

"It's hard to watch back but also gives me that fire in the belly."

Clarke climbed off the canvas twice before dramatically halting Jack Massey in his last fight in June.

But he insists his boxing intelligence along with his battling spirit will be crucial in the fight with Billam-Smith.

"I didn't learn nothing new about myself in Bournemouth," he said. "I know that once I'm in the ring or when I'm in any situation, you've got to stop me to stop me. If you get me down, you got to keep me down.

"Billam-Smith is notoriously tough, but boxing is not a game to be tough. It's not a tough person's sport. It's a smart person's sport, so we'll see."

articles.summary: El máximo activo de Zuffa Boxing, Shakur Stevenson, llega a un acuerdo para abandonar la promotora sin haber peleado ni una sola vez para esta

El campeón en cuatro divisiones subió al ring por última vez en enero pasado en un combate en el que dominó como quiso a Teófimo López. En los últimos meses se habló de un posible combate primero contra Conor Benn y recientemente se había vinculado a Shakur con un posible enfrentamiento con Devin Haney. De hecho, entablaron negociaciones entre ambas partes que no fructificaron. El habilidoso zurdo de Newark se queja de que lleva ocho semanas en un campamento de entrenamiento preparándose para combates que nunca tienen lugar. Así lo ha explicado el propio Stevenson: "He estado trabajando hasta el cansancio, manteniéndome enfocado, manteniéndome en forma. Llevo de campamento como ocho semanas preparándome para peleas que me dijeron que iban a suceder y no han sucedido”, explica el púgil. Prosigue así: “Este es el negocio del boxeo. No estoy enfadado con nadie, no estoy señalando con el dedo. A pesar de todos estos problemas y cosas que han estado pasando, he solicitado ser liberado de Zuffa Boxing. El fin de semana, mi solicitud fue concedida y ahora oficialmente soy agente libre”. Finalmente, Shakur abre las puertas a negociar con otros promotores: “Esta vez quiero decirle a los fans que mi carrera está en mis propias manos y estoy empezando mi propia compañía promotora y estoy dispuesto a trabajar con otros promotores y cualquiera más que esté dispuesto a ser serio sobre mi carrera como yo lo soy". Qué está pasando con Zuffa Boxing no lo sabemos, pero acaba de dejar escapar a su mayor activo.

articles.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Zuffa Boxing exit exposes further flaws in Dana White’s grand plan
articles.summary: Zuffa Boxing promised to “fix boxing.” Now its biggest star signing has left without throwing a single punch.
articles.body:
Shakur Stevenson has announced his Zuffa Boxing exit just 101 days after signing a reported "multi-fight deal" with Dana White's promotional outfit — all without throwing a single punch .

The news came via the YouTube channel of the unbeaten 29-year-old on Monday afternoon, pulling the plug on his relationship with Zuffa Boxing, seemingly, following the breakdown of a failed fight with Devin Haney.

The two unbeaten Americans had been circling a potential showdown later this year, but negotiations ultimately became bogged down by disagreements over the weight and a proposed rehydration clause.

It signals yet another blow for Zuffa Boxing and White, who promised to "fix boxing" when they entered the sport full-time at the start of 2026.

"I've been working my ass off, staying focused, I've been in camp for eight weeks preparing for fights I was told would happen but have not happened," Stevenson explained Monday.

"It is what it is, this is the business of boxing, I'm not mad at anyone, but I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing and over the weekend my request was granted.

"I'm officially a free agent," the WBO super lightweight champion continued. "I'm now taking my career into my own hands, starting my own promotional company, and I'm willing to work with other promoters that are willing to be serious about my career.

"I want the biggest fights available at 135 pounds or 140 pounds, where I hold my title."

Stevenson also stated that he plans to make a future move to the welterweight division.

"None of these guys can beat me. And give it a year or two, we'll get to 147 pounds," he said. "I will get there, but on my time, not on anyone else's. I'll be the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter soon and I'm open to co-promoting and working with any of the networks."

Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs), Uncrowned's No. 4 pound-for-pound boxer in the world . has clearly reached breaking point after a frustrating 2026.

The WBO super lightweight champion has not fought since beating Teofimo Lopez to claim the title in January. After signing with Zuffa Boxing in July , Stevenson appeared to be entering a new chapter of his career.

Instead, he has turned his back on White's outfit after the company failed to get a big fight over the line for him.

For a promotion that has consistently extolled a supposed ability to cut through boxing's usual red tape, it's an awkward early setback. Signing one of the sport's most talented fighters is one thing. Delivering the fights he wants is quite another.

White has spent years criticizing boxing's fragmented promotional landscape. Too many belts, too many competing interests, too many fights that should happen but never do.

His pitch was simple: Bring the sport into a more organized system, put the best against the best and use the resources of Saudi Arabia's Sela and TKO — the parent company of the UFC and WWE — to make it happen.

Stevenson was, on paper, the perfect signing to sell that vision. An undefeated, American, four-division world champion, one of the most technically gifted fighters of his generation. A man who had made no secret of his desire to face the biggest names available in boxing.

Yet the first major test of that promise has ended with one of Zuffa's most valuable assets heading for the exit.

Of course, there are always two sides to every story. And in boxing, there are often more than that — somewhere in the middle lies the truth.

We haven't yet heard White or Zuffa Boxing's side to this story, but if, as predicted, they claim Stevenson was being unreasonable with some his demands, financial or otherwise, it's hard to justify their hesitance considering the money they have already spent in 2026.

Conor Benn signed an agreement with the organization worth a reported value of $15 million for an appearance against Regis Prograis on the Fury vs. Makhmudov undercard, so surely the scope was there to overpay for one of the sport's biggest stars?

If money is the issue, it would be remiss not to cite the ongoing question marks hanging over Saudi Arabia's investment in sport .

Zuffa Boxing is not simply a Dana White operation with UFC branding attached. It was established through a partnership between TKO and Saudi Arabia's Sela, with Turki Alalshikh, chairman of the Saudi General Entertainment Authority, among its leading figures. Saudi backing has been central to the venture from the outset.

Saudi Arabia has transformed boxing's financial landscape over the past few years, but the question of longevity has always remained: What happens when the taps turn off?

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has decided to stop funding LIV Golf after its current season, prompting wider questions about the sustainability of its international sporting investments under its new 2026-30 strategy. This isn't to suggest that boxing is also imminently for the chop, but it wouldn't be hyperbolic to suggest that the honeymoon period Saudi Arabia's relationship with boxing is over. Welcome to the humdrum of marriage.

Spencer Brown, the longtime manager of Tyson Fury, told Uncrowned just last week that he expects December's Fury vs. Anthony Joshua bout to be "one of the last of the big fights" Saudi Arabia may finance. "Everything has to calm down," Brown said. "The money has to go down because nobody can keep paying that sort of money."

Whether Stevenson's departure serves as a red flag for other potential Zuffa Boxing recruits remains to be seen.

The coming months will tell us plenty. White has repeatedly urged the boxing world to "judge us on our body of work" after 12 months in the game. Well, as we hurtle through the fall, it is difficult to imagine a bigger story threatening to overshadow Zuffa Boxing's early progress.

For a promotion that promised to cut through boxing's B.S., losing one of its biggest signings before he's even fought under its banner is hardly the sort of work White had in mind.

Now, the challenge for White and Zuffa Boxing is this: Can they "fix boxing" without just throwing money at it? If it took just over three months for Stevenson to turn away, what exactly is this revolution offering — and, perhaps more importantly, what is it failing to deliver?

articles.title: Incêndios no Amazonas: Aeronaves lançam 1 milhão de litros de água | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre os equipamentos utilizados estão os aviões KC-390, equipados com o Sistema Modular Aerotransportável de Combate a Incêndios. Segundo as informações divulgadas pelo governo federal, o sistema permite lançar grandes volumes de água em cerca de sete segundos.
articles.summary: Aviões KC-390 e brigadistas reforçam o combate aos incêndios no Amazonas com tecnologia que lança grandes volumes de água em poucos segundos para conter as chamas.
articles.body:
Aeronave do Ibama lança água sobre área de incêndio no Amazonas — Foto: Rogério Cassimiro/MMA

Aeronaves mobilizadas pelo governo federal lançaram mais de 1,1 milhão de litros de água para combater incêndios florestais no Amazonas desde 10 de outubro. Os dados são do Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA). As operações somam 390,5 horas de voo e 369 lançamentos de água . Segundo o balanço, 337 ocorrências de incêndio foram extintas desde o início da temporada.

Atualmente, 13 aeronaves federais participam das operações . São seis aviões Air Tractor, usados para lançar água sobre as áreas atingidas, cinco helicópteros, que transportam equipes e equipamentos e também auxiliam no combate ao fogo, e dois aviões KC-390, da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB).

As equipes também contam com 462 brigadistas do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama) e do Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade ( ICMBio ), além de 54 militares da FAB e 41 integrantes da Força Nacional . A operação inclui ainda o apoio à contratação de 116 bombeiros do Amazonas.

O trabalho em terra é apoiado por 58 veículos e nove embarcações, usados no transporte de equipes e equipamentos e no monitoramento das áreas atingidas. As aeronaves ajudam principalmente no combate às chamas em regiões de difícil acesso.

Aviões podem lançar milhares de litros de água em segundos

Entre os equipamentos utilizados estão os aviões KC-390 , equipados com o Sistema Modular Aerotransportável de Combate a Incêndios (MAFFS, na sigla em inglês).

Segundo as informações divulgadas pelo governo federal, o sistema permite lançar grandes volumes de água em cerca de sete segundos.

Entre as ações estão a instalação de um Estado-Maior Conjunto das Forças Armadas na capital, para coordenar as operações militares, e a implantação de uma base da Força Nacional do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), prevista para terça-feira (20), para reforçar o atendimento à população.

O governo também anunciou a ampliação do apoio financeiro ao estado e aos municípios e a mobilização de órgãos de segurança para investigar possíveis crimes relacionados aos incêndios.

Entre 12 e 18 de outubro, o Amazonas registrou 548 focos de calor, 470 a menos que nos sete dias anteriores , segundo dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais ( Inpe ).

Itacoatiara liderou o número de registros no período, com 59 focos . Em seguida, aparecem Autazes , com 46 , e Boa Vista do Ramos , com 39 .

Uso do fogo é proibido durante emergência

No Amazonas, o uso do fogo está proibido durante a vigência do decreto estadual de emergência, independentemente da finalidade . Quem descumprir a medida pode ser responsabilizado.

A legislação brasileira também estabelece restrições ao uso do fogo na vegetação por causa dos riscos de incêndios, destruição de áreas naturais, degradação do solo e poluição do ar, que pode prejudicar a saúde da população.

O Código Florestal, instituído pela Lei nº 12.651/2012, proíbe o uso do fogo na vegetação, salvo nas exceções previstas em lei. Já a Lei nº 14.944/2024 criou a Política Nacional de Manejo Integrado do Fogo e estabeleceu regras para o uso controlado do fogo.

articles.title: Ian Machado Garry Scheduled for UFC Return
articles.summary: UFC welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry is scheduled to make his return to the Octagon before the end of 2026. Machado Garry was last seen at UFC 330 in...
articles.body:
UFC welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry is scheduled to make his return to the Octagon before the end of 2026.

Machado Garry was last seen at UFC 330 in August, when he lost a unanimous decision to UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev in a fight that UFC president Dana White criticized the Irishman for a lack of action during the bout.

Just a few months later, it appears that Machado Garry is set to return to the Octagon to try to get the bitter taste of defeat to Makhachev out of his mouth.

Ian Machado Garry Rumored for Quick UFC Return

Per Ariel Helwani, Machado Garry will likely fight again before the end of the year, though no opponent or exact date and location were named.

Taking a look at the UFC welterweight division, there are several opponents who could make sense for him.

One potential opponent who has called Machado Garry out for several months on social media is Michael Morales , the undefeated knockout artist who is itching to get back into the Octagon, as he hasn't fought since a UFC 322 knockout win over Sean Brady, which was nearly a year ago at this point.

Though Morales has been linked to a welterweight matchup against Shavkat Rakhmonov, there is no certainty that Rakhmonov is healthy and ready to return after missing the last two years due to injury. If he is healthy, then he should fight Morales for a No. 1 contender spot at 170 lbs, as Carlos Prates is likely going to be the next man in line to fight Makhachev for the belt.

Another potential fight for Machado Garry could be a fight against former UFC welterweight champion Jack Della Maddalena, who hasn't fought since May, when he was knocked out by Prates.

Either way, despite a lackluster fight against Makhachev that White and the UFC brass clearly did not care for, Machado Garry is still one of the top-ranked welterweights in the sport today, and he will likely fight someone in the top five for his next fight as he climbs back into title contention.

articles.title: Is Petr Yan the Greatest Boxer in UFC History? Promotion Seems to Think So
articles.summary: Ahead of his UFC 333 title trilogy with Merab Dvalishvili, the official UFC YouTube channel has paid a special tribute to the Russian.
articles.body:
In less than a week, Petr Yan will put his bantamweight title on the line against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333. The rivals are set to complete their trilogy in Abu Dhabi, with both fighters having one win apiece heading into the decisive showdown.

Dvalishvili dominated their first meeting in March 2023, securing a convincing decision victory with his relentless pressure and wrestling. However, Yan turned things around at UFC 323 in December 2025, shutting down the Georgian's grappling-heavy approach to earn a lopsided decision win and reclaim the bantamweight championship.

With fight week underway, the UFC has found a way to celebrate Yan's return to the top. The promotion recently uploaded a video titled "UFC's Greatest Boxer ," featuring more than three hours of the Russian's best moments inside the Octagon.

UFC Honors Petr Yan With Massive Career Compilation Ahead of Merab Dvalishvili Trilogy

The tribute, posted on the UFC's official YouTube channel, highlights Yan's standout performances against some of the division's biggest names, including Jose Aldo, Urijah Faber, Cory Sandhagen, Song Yadong, and Marcus McGhee.

Yan's boxing is a big reason why he has earned such a reputation. The Russian uses a high guard to block and parry incoming shots while steadily moving forward. He also switches between orthodox and southpaw stances with ease, creating different angles for his attacks and setting up powerful body hooks and sharp counterpunches.

His numbers back up his reputation, too. Yan boasts a 55% striking accuracy rate, landing 1,456 of his 2,652 significant strike attempts. He also lands 5.16 significant strikes per minute while maintaining a 60% striking defense rate.

The Russian has recorded nine knockdowns at bantamweight, tied for the most in the division's history, and holds the UFC record for the most significant strikes landed in the weight class. Of course, calling Yan the UFC's greatest boxer is bound to spark some debate.

Fighters such as Max Holloway and Dustin Poirier have strong cases of their own, thanks to their striking records and performances against elite competition.

However, Yan's biggest strength lies in his technical fundamentals. Rather than relying solely on volume, he patiently studies his opponents, switches stances to create openings, and uses sharp combinations and intelligent footwork to cut off the Octagon. His defensive awareness also makes him difficult to hit cleanly.

Still, the UFC's bold praise might not convince everyone. Yan hasn't finished an opponent since 2020, giving critics another reason to question the label. With his trilogy fight against Dvalishvili just days away, the Russian will have another opportunity to remind fans why his boxing remains one of the best in the sport.

articles.title: World champion Shakur Stevenson 'granted' release from Dana White's Zuffa Boxing
articles.summary: Four-weight world champion Shakur Stevenson signed for Dana White's Zuffa Boxing in July but says promised fights have not materialised.
articles.body:
Shakur Stevenson says he has secured a release from Zuffa Boxing without fighting for the promotion.

Multiple-weight world champion Stevenson, 29, was one of several high-profile signings for the Saudi Arabian-backed boxing promotion headed by UFC owners TKO and Dana White.

He was in talks to fight WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney but those discussions appear to have broken down – with Stevenson saying he was now a "free agent".

"I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing," Stevenson said on his Youtube channel.

"Now, over the weekend, my request has been granted."

Zuffa Boxing has not comment on Stevenson's suggested exit from the promotion.

White has vowed to take over boxing and his most eye-catching signing was that of Conor Benn, poaching the Briton from Matchroom and Eddie Hearn.

Benn has now had two fights with Zuffa, the second being last month's quick knockout defeat by world champion Ryan Garcia.

Stevenson's last outing was an impressive win against American rival Teofimo Lopez, when he became a four-weight world champion.

The New Jersey native was keen to be become a five-weight world champion by fighting Haney, but Stevenson says he has been left frustrated by being on the sidelines since signing with Zuffa in July.

"I've been in camp for like eight weeks, preparing for fights that I was told was going to happen and have not happened," Stevenson said.

"It is what it is. This is the business of boxing. I'm not mad at anyone, I'm not pointing fingers.

"I am taking my career in my own hands and starting my own promotional company and I'm willing to work with other promoters and anybody else that's willing to be as serious about my career as I am," he added.

Stevenson says he now plans to defend his WBO light-welterweight world title before moving up to welterweight in the coming years.

articles.title: Maniobra viral: se hace el muerto para escapar de un estrangulamiento y acaba ganando el combate
articles.standfirst: El japonés Seiya Sugimoto engañó a Takeru Suzuki en el primer asalto y se impuso por decisión unánime después de tres rounds
articles.summary: El japonés Seiya Sugimoto engañó a Takeru Suzuki en el primer asalto y se impuso por decisión unánime después de tres rounds
articles.body: Seiya Sugimoto encontró una salida inesperada cuando Takeru Suzuki le tenía atrapado en un estrangulamiento por la espalda: fingió haber perdido el conocimiento. Su rival aflojó la presión, el árbitro no detuvo el combate y el japonés aprovechó ese instante para liberarse. La maniobra le permitió continuar una pelea que terminó ganando por decisión unánime este lunes en Japón, según informa RMC Sport. El apuro llegó en el primer asalto. Suzuki había colocado a su compatriota en una situación comprometida y tenía a su alcance resolver el combate. Sugimoto simuló entonces un desvanecimiento y consiguió que su adversario soltara el agarre antes de que el árbitro hubiera decretado el final. Con la pelea todavía en marcha, escapó y pudo disputar los tres asaltos, al término de los cuales los jueces le dieron la victoria. Era su séptimo triunfo desde su debut profesional en 2022. Después del combate, el propio Sugimoto describió su recurso con la expresión francesa que recoge RMC Sport, "faire le mort", hacerse el muerto. También precisó que seguía algo aturdido. La secuencia concentró buena parte de las reacciones de los observadores, aunque el resto de la pelea también dejó momentos espectaculares. De policía a profesional del MMA Sugimoto tiene 34 años y fue policía antes de dedicarse profesionalmente a las artes marciales mixtas. Dio ese paso a los 30 y está vinculado a The Blackbelt Japan. Compite en el peso mosca, categoría en la que este lunes añadió una nueva victoria a su trayectoria tras superar aquel estrangulamiento del primer asalto. Suzuki terminó la jornada con un balance de cinco victorias y dos derrotas. Entre quienes comentaron la acción hubo sorpresa por su decisión de aflojar el agarre: el estrangulamiento por la espalda es precisamente una de sus especialidades para ganar combates. Frente a Sugimoto, soltó la presión con el árbitro todavía sin intervenir.

articles.title: Ibai, ¿por qué no devuelves al boxeo lo que te ha dado?
articles.summary: La opinión de Emilio Marquiegui
articles.body: El comunicador Ibai Llanos, gracias a un tremendo esfuerzo, ha llegado muy alto en su actividad. El trabajo que tienen detrás estos llamados 'influencers' o 'streamers' es enorme, pocos imaginan el sacrificio para alcanzar la cima. Y una de las mejores iniciativas y éxitos del vizcaíno ha sido la llamada 'Velada del Año'. Desde 2021, con un atractivo formato pugilístico, diversas celebridades resuelven sus rencillas en el ring con los guantes de cuero. ¿Por qué discutir, pudiéndolo arreglar con los puños? Simpático aforismo que empleamos en el boxeo. Desde luego, personalmente nunca he criticado ese espectáculo, porque, aunque no da, no quita, la gente se acerca al boxeo, los protagonistas del evento aprenden pugilismo, fomentan el fantástico ejercicio boxístico en los gimnasios, y pensamos que ayuda a la popularidad de nuestro deporte. Ahora, la cadena Netflix apoya el formato, buena noticia. Si ya tenía un gran éxito La Velada del Año, este acompañamiento la propulsará aún más lejos. Y creo que es el momento de un paso al frente, quedarse en las cuerdas no mejora las cosas. Ibai Llanos debería plantearse devolver el apoyo del boxeo, ayudarlo realmente. El legendario deporte del golpeo y la esquiva, sus reglas, su estructura, su fama, han ayudado mucho. ¿Y si devolvemos la contribución? ¿Qué tal la inclusión de algún emocionante combate profesional con alguna de nuestras estrellas? Si tu colega Jake Paul lo ha hecho, ¿Por qué no Ibai? Un campeonato mundial sería lo máximo, pero, por ejemplo, una eliminatoria entre el número 2 del Consejo Mundial de Boxeo (WBC), tu amigo Sandor Martín, y el número 12 de la misma organización, tu paisano, el también 'streamer' Jon Fernández, sería fantástico. Duelo nacional como antesala de un campeonato del mundo. Pero también hay otros combates entre españoles que aportarían una elegancia y notoriedad que miles de nuevos seguidores valorarían mucho. Primero vendría la curiosidad por los enfrentamientos entre esos afamados novatos y después la ansiada llegada de los profesionales, el momento de algún duelo soñado por los fans que se podría donar a la extenuada afición española, que necesita vitaminas para mantener la alegría. Y podría ser organizando esos combates con la triple i: interés deportivo, ilusión por el enfrentamiento e incertidumbre sobre el resultado. Algo que podría convertir La Velada del Año en La Velada del Siglo. O en algo que sonaría tan dulce como La Balada del Año. Hazlo, Ibai.

articles.title: Former boxing world champion Joe Cordina cleared of assault after punching man
articles.summary: The judge said she was satisfied the boxer was defending himself during the incident.
articles.body:
Former boxing world champion Joe Cordina has been cleared of assaulting a man he punched outside a petrol station.

The incident outside a garage in Pentwyn, Cardiff, in February led to the 34-year-old being denied entry to the US for a WBO lightweight title clash.

District Judge Charlotte Murphy found Cordina not guilty of assault by beating against Jamie O'Brien, 33, following a trial at Cardiff Magistrates' Court.

"I am further satisfied that a single, measured, controlled punch was proportionate in the circumstances," she said.

"It is very easy to consider the defendant's response by considering the CCTV in slow motion, however the defendant had a split second to consider his response to the shoulder barge."

After the hearing, Cordina said in a statement on social media that he was "hugely relieved" to put the incident behind him and was now focused "firmly on the future and getting back in the ring".

Cordina had been filling up his Land Rover before he approached O'Brien, who had been sitting on the pavement near the petrol station exit.

CCTV footage showed O'Brien pushing Cordina using his shoulder, before the two-time IBF super-featherweight champion punched him with sufficient force to knock him to the ground.

The pair continued to "remonstrate" with one another and exchange blows.

Police began to investigate the incident after footage of the altercation was circulated online.

Cordina said he initially thought O'Brien was a fan who wanted a photograph.

He called him over, but O'Brien said: "You come here."

Cordina said O'Brien then "barged" him during their initial interaction and left him feeling threatened.

"He had his hands in his pockets, I don't know what people carry on them these days," he added.

The judge said: "In my view, it was necessary and the force used was proportionate in the circumstances.

"I reject any suggestion that the defendant was retaliating in any way.

"This is a person who has lived in the public eye for many years and has interacted with the public on a daily basis.

"For all of those reasons, the crown has not proved to the criminal standard. I therefore find the defendant not guilty and dismiss the charge."

The judge had previously ruled there was no case to answer in relation to the second charge of assault.

Cordina told the court it was "pretty much" a certainty that he would risk losing his boxing licence if he received a criminal conviction and that this "100%" had an impact on how he conducted himself day to day.

In a statement posted on Instagram on Tuesday, Cordina said it had been a "difficult period" for him and those close to him.

He thanked his lawyer, his family and friends and "everyone who stood by me".

"Your loyalty and support have meant a great deal to me," he said.

"Boxing has been my life for as long as I can remember, and I'm looking forward to putting all my energy into training, preparing for my next fight and doing what I love."

articles.title: Rajada tras no ser renovado por UFC: "Están creando una base de fans..."
articles.standfirst: Farid Basharat se ha mostrado en desacuerdo con la decisión de la compañía al tener un récord invicto
articles.summary: Farid Basharat se ha mostrado en desacuerdo con la decisión de la compañía al tener un récord invicto
articles.body: Uno de los temas más comentados en el mundo de las MMA durante la semana pasada es la no renovación de Farid Basharat (16-0) con la UFC. Según informó el propio peleador, la compañía dirigida por Dana White ha decidido dejar de contar con sus servicios a pesar de tener un récord invicto, algo que ha generado diversidad de opiniones y que ha provocado una dura crítica hacia la compañía por parte del propio peleador, que sigue sin entender lo sucedido. Farid llegó a la UFC en 2022 a través de las Dana White's Contender Series, donde no te vale solo con ganar para conseguir un contrato. Es decir, que a Dana White le gustó la actuación de Basharat y decidió darle una oportunidad. Desde entonces, el peleador nacido en Afganistán ha sumado siete victorias, aunque solo una finalización, lo que según muchos ha podido llevar a la compañía a tomar esta decisión hacia el peleador de peso gallo. Al igual que le pasó a su hermano hace unos meses, que también fue despedido, ahora Farid le tocará buscar una nueva compañía para mostrar su talento, aunque no se ha quedado callado al respecto. "Creo que la UFC está creando una base de aficionados que no aprecia los combates de buena calidad. Aunque sea un combate desigual, aunque sea un combate de bajo nivel, siempre que haya sangre o finalización en el primer asalto estamos contentos", afirmó en sus redes sociales. De hecho, Basharat fue más allá y añadió que "no se puede construir un deporte sobre esa base, porque puede que te vaya bien en cuanto a índices de audiencia un par de años, pero tarde o temprano eso deslegitimará el deporte, y los aficionados se quedarán con ganas de combates de verdad. Cuando vea a los mejores enfrentarse entre sí, eso es lo que resulta entretenido. Pero la UFC tiene garantizados 7.700 millones en siete años, así que está claro que son muy buenos en lo que hacen", finalizó. Lo cierto es que el propio Dana White fue preguntado al respecto tras el UFC Edmonton de este finde, y dejó caer que esta decisión va más allá del plano deportivo. "Si tienes un récord de 16-0, con siete victorias en la UFC, y no te renuevan el contrato, sin duda hay una razón". El jefe de la compañía no es el único que se ha pronunciado al respecto, ya que entre los propios peleadores hay una gran diversidad de opiniones. Están los que apelan a la meritocracia y a sus buenos resultados para dejar caer que no todo vale, y los que opinan que esto es un negocio y tienes que vender tus peleas bien para que no se den estas situaciones. De hecho, no es un caso aislado, ya que ha ocurrido con más peleadores. Farid no cierra la puerta a volver a la UFC en un futuro, como ya hicieron otros nombres como Brandon Moreno o Kyle Daukaus, pero sabe que tiene muy complicado que esto suceda. Además, ha sido de los pocos que ha alzado la voz de esta manera tras conocer su no continuación en la compañía, por lo que su relación con Dana White y su equipo no debe ser la mejor del mundo.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois: Fight with Tyson Fury next year would be 'ground-breaking' | 'That'll be the next level for me'
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois, the WBO heavyweight world champion, is eyeing a showdown with Tyson Fury next year; "Fury's a fighting man, I'm sure he would want it. Let's see how he does with AJ," Dubois said; After crushing Fabio Wardley in a rematch, Dubois hopes to go into a unification fight next
articles.body:
Dubois swept through Fabio Wardley in two rounds of their rematch on Saturday to defend the WBO heavyweight championship.

Fury has his all-British super-fight with Anthony Joshua in December. If he beats Joshua he'd win the WBA 'super' title and Dubois would relish a unification clash with Fury.

"Definitely. That'll be ground-breaking. That'll be the next level for me," Dubois told Sky Sports .

"I've fought everyone then really from this era. I've fought them all. Fury's the last one.

"Fury's a fighting man, I'm sure he would want it. Let's see how he does with AJ. Let's see. I'm sure Frank [Warren, who promotes Fury and Dubois] would love to make that fight."

Dubois has twice headlined at Wembley Stadium against Anthony Joshua and then Oleksandr Usyk. Fury versus Dubois would fill any stadium.

"This is what boxing is. This is the highest level really, this is it at the highest level. This is what it looks like," Dubois said.

Fury and Dubois do have a past. They sparred briefly many years ago. "That was just when I was turning pro," Dubois said. "I went to spar his cousin Hughie and then he popped in for a few rounds. Great memories, great work."

It was when Fury was returning to boxing after ballooning in weight. "So he was massive then," he said, but added with a laugh: "He was elusive."

Dubois fell short in his undisputed championship fight with Usyk but he remains determined to scale the summit of the heavyweight division.

"To win all the belts. That's the main thing now for me, collecting all the other belts," he said. "It would mean everything to have all those belts. No one can take that away from me. That's what I'm after now.

"Amongst all the names of history, not just that, for myself and what's left to achieve in boxing as well."

After only being taken two rounds in his last fight, Dubois wants to box again "soon, really soon. I want to be out soon, as soon as possible. Whenever the belts are ready, whenever the top challengers are ready, that's what I want. I want to fight".

Dubois is hoping his next opponent will be WBC titlist Agit Kabayel or IBF belt-holder Filip Hrgovic, whom Dubois has beaten before.

"Any one of them [next], Hrgovic, he was there on Saturday, maybe him or Kabayel," he said. "Hrgovic was tough as well, Kabayel, we'll see, we'll see what he's about. He ain't been in with a guy like me but he's a good fighter.

"Just anyone with a damn belt… Anyone who wants it."

articles.title: Joe Cordina: Former boxing world champion cleared of assaulting man he punched outside petrol station
articles.summary: Two-time IBF super-featherweight champion Joe Cordina has been cleared of assaulting a man he punched outside a petrol station; a district judge found Cordina, 34, not guilty of assault
articles.body:
A district judge found Cordina, 34, not guilty of assault by beating against Jamie O'Brien, 33, following a trial at Cardiff Magistrates' Court.

The court heard Cordina had been filling up his Land Rover at Pentwyn service station in Cardiff in February when he noticed O'Brien staring at him.

Cordina, a two-time IBF super-featherweight champion, approached O'Brien - who was sitting on the pavement near the station exit - believing he was a fan.

Judge Charlotte Murphy described how O'Brien then "shoulder barged him to the chest and chin", in what she found was a "deliberate assault" on Cordina.

She highlighted that the attack had taken place just two weeks after Cordina had been told by police that there was a threat to his life.

In her ruling, the judge said: "I am satisfied that the defendant believed it was necessary to use force to defend himself.

"I am further satisfied that a single, measured, controlled punch was proportionate in the circumstances.

"It is very easy to consider the defendant's response by considering the CCTV in slow motion, however the defendant had a split second to consider his response to the shoulder barge."

The judge said she accepted Cordina's evidence that he had repeatedly pushed O'Brien "while on the floor to keep him away from him".

"In my view, it was necessary and the force used was proportionate in the circumstances," she added.

"I reject any suggestion that the defendant was retaliating in any way.

"This is a person who has lived in the public eye for many years and has interacted with the public on a daily basis.

"For all of those reasons, the crown has not proved to the criminal standard. I therefore find the defendant not guilty and dismiss the charge."

The judge had previously ruled there was no case to answer in relation to the second charge of assault.

CCTV footage played to the court showed O'Brien pushing Cordina with his shoulder, before Cordina punched him.

O'Brien, from Pentwyn, previously pleaded guilty to a charge of assault by beating.

Police began to investigate the incident after footage was circulated online. The judge ruled on Tuesday there was no evidence that O'Brien knew the person who was filming.

She added that Cordina had approached O'Brien "in good faith", believing he was a fan.

During the trial, Cordina said he initially thought O'Brien wanted a photograph and described how he was accustomed to being recognised four or five times a day.

He told the court he had acted in self-defence because he felt threatened after O'Brien assaulted him.

"He had his hands in his pockets, I don't know what people carry on them these days," Cordina said.

After the case, Cordina's lawyer Nadeem Majid issued a statement to the media.

He said: "Today's verdict is a huge relief for Joe and everybody who is close to him.

"He has always maintained he is innocent throughout this.

"On behalf of Joe, I'd like to thank his family, his friends, his loyal fans, his legal team for their unwavering support through what's clearly been a very difficult time.

"Joe would now like to concentrate on his family and in particular his boxing. We'd all like to see him on the bill in December. Thank you all very much."

articles.title: EA Sports Announces Return of 'Fight Night' Boxing Video Game, 'The Fight Is Never Over'
articles.summary: Retro gaming fans were given a treat on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Retro gaming fans were given a treat on Tuesday.

EA Sports announced that it is reviving its famed Fight Night video game series, declaring, "The fight is never over."

Fight Night followed EA Sports' previous boxing series, Knockout Kings , and had five editions produced for various platforms between 2004 and 2011. The series was critically acclaimed and a staple at the top of the sales charts.

Mike Straw of Insider Gaming reported last month that sources said plans for a Fight Night reboot were canceled. However, EA Sports' sale to a group led by the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund left some hope alive because of the PIF's "major stake in boxing."

The return of Fight Night comes at a booming period for video games. EA Sports has already revived its college football series and launched the sixth edition of its UFC series earlier this year. Rockstar's highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI is coming next month and reportedly has already generated over $600 million in pre-sales alone.

EA Sports was also likely influenced to bring back Fight Night after seeing the popularity of the Steel City Interactive boxing video game Undisputed , which was the first licensed boxing game since Fight Night 's last release in 2011.

Fans will certainly be excited to see the continued development of EA Sports' Fight Night reboot before its much-anticipated release.

articles.standfirst: El mexicano se enfrenta el 31 de octubre a Christian Mbili y 'Bud' ve a su antiguo adversario saliendo con el brazo en alto
articles.summary: El mexicano se enfrenta el 31 de octubre a Christian Mbili y 'Bud' ve a su antiguo adversario saliendo con el brazo en alto
articles.body: Canelo Álvarez (63-3-2, 39 KO) regresará en poco más de una semana al ring, en la que será su primera pelea desde la derrota ante Terence Crawford. El tapatío se medirá al invicto Christian Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KO), quien protagonizó un combate durísimo contra Lester Martínez en aquella misma velada y que terminó en un empate por decisión dividida. Tras este combate, Canelo pasó por el quirófano para operarse del codo y actualmente entrena junto a su inseparable Eddy Reynoso y el equipo de Oleksandr Usyk. En breve el mexicano se trasladará a Riad, aunque la situación en la capital de Arabia Saudí sigue siendo de inestabilidad debido a los bombardeos de los hutíes, que ya han dejado varias víctimas. En declaraciones a DAZN Boxing, se le preguntó a Crawford qué consejo le daría a Mbili de cara al combate de su vida. “No puedo, porque el estilo hace las peleas. Su estilo está hecho a medida para Canelo. No puede hacer otra cosa que presionarlo. No lo veo venciendo a Canelo en un combate de boxeo. Su mayor éxito será soltar sus puños, castigarlo y convertirlo en una batalla campal”. Recordemos que Mbilli fue elevado a campeón del supermedio por el Consejo Mundial de Boxeo (WBC) después de defender su título interino ante Lester Martínez, por lo que Canelo tendrá la opción de recuperar el cinturón que le arrebató Crawford. Por su parte, el púgil francés residente en Canadá y nacido en Camerún ha ganado 29 de sus 30 peleas, pero lo cierto es que nunca se ha enfrentado a nadie del nivel de Álvarez. Como dice ‘Bud’, le interesa una pelea muy dura y física.

articles.title: Daniel Richardson: “No hago esto por fama o dinero, es algo que me trae paz y felicidad”

El peleador del Climent Club, consolidado con un interesante 3-0 en su carrera como profesional, peleará este fin de semana en WOW 33 Vitoria contra el durísimo Willmar Quirama (4-0-1) en una prueba de nivel para saber a qué puede aspirar Richardson. En la previa de este combate, atiende a MARCA.
articles.body: Dos años después, Daniel Richardson (3-0) regresa a WOW FC. El peleador del Climent Club, consolidado con un interesante 3-0 en su carrera como profesional, peleará este fin de semana en WOW 33 Vitoria contra el durísimo Willmar Quirama (4-0-1) en una prueba de nivel para saber a qué puede aspirar Richardson. En la previa de este combate, atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. Por fin llega a WOW. ¿Cómo ha vivido estos meses desde que se anunció su fichaje? Respuesta. La verdad que sé de la pelea ya 11 semanas atrás. Así que he tenido un muy buen ‘training camp’. Es algo que siempre da gusto, ¿no?, que no sea algo en corto aviso. Y muy bien, la verdad que creo que he crecido bastante estas semanas como peleador. El reto de pelear con Quirama, volver a WOW… un poquito la situación cambiante me ha hecho exigirme aún más en los entrenamientos. Así que muy bien, la verdad. P. Hay muchas expectativas por verle pelear… R. No le doy mucha importancia en el sentido de que yo también quiero verme pelear. Al final esto es mi vida, mi día a día, lo que yo hago, por todo lo que he trabajado… así que todo lo que hay externo, el ruido… no es algo que me quite el sueño la verdad. Yo hago esto por y para mí, y para mi familia y la gente que me quiere. Es verdad que agradezco la atención, agradezco la presión en ese sentido, ¿no?, pero me parece un privilegio que ocurre cuando creo que haces las cosas bien, cuando la gente espera cosas de ti… si nadie espera nada de mí sería un poco estar haciendo las cosas mal. Así que más que sentirlo como presión lo agradezco, me parece algo positivo. P. Pero para el Climent Club siempre ha habido muchos focos. ¿Se han acostumbrado ya a eso? R. Llevo compitiendo desde que tengo 12 años así que el competir no es algo tampoco que me suponga algo súper estresante y también a lo mejor mi perspectiva de cómo veo el mundo no sé… siento que todos vamos a morir en menos de 60-70 años, ¿no?. Sé que es un poco cínico, pero no le doy la importancia a lo mejor a lo que otras personas le darían. Me parece la vida como unos años que tenemos aquí en este mundo, en esta vida para aprender y no la voy a vivir perdiendo el tiempo… así que no vería como como fallar nada de lo que pasa en mi vida. Yo lo doy absolutamente todo en mi día a día, persigo mis sueños, pienso que voy a cumplirlos y si no los cumplo pues no me quedaré con la duda. Ese es mi pensamiento, entonces no me pongo presión extra con pensamientos ajenos. P. ¿Mantener el invicto supone presión? R. Eso lo decide Dios, yo soy creyente y entonces pienso que es algo ajeno. Ya no me pesa, con el tiempo como peleador estoy madurando. Antes, como amateur, quizás pensaba eso de ‘buah, no puedo perder’... pero es que a día de hoy ya lo tengo como algo muy natural. Cada vez las peleas van a ser de más nivel y creo que todo el mundo cae en este deporte tarde o temprano si se queda el tiempo suficiente peleando. P. ¿Por qué WOW ahora? R. Es el momento. Ya necesitaba retos, necesitaba sentir que estaba avanzando realmente en mi carrera. Al final es verdad que las primeras peleas no me importaba dónde pelear, quería simplemente coger un poco de experiencia en la jaula con los rounds de 5 minutos, con las guantillas de 4 onzas, con los codos… pero ya después de tres peleas creo que el colchón por así decir de experiencia está ahí. P. Quirama, que también está invicto, es una prueba muy dura para arrancar. R. A mí me gusta. Me parece una buena pelea. De hecho, cuando era el número uno del ranking WOW amateur y vi a Quirama pelear una noche… dije que quería pelear con él. Eso fue en 2024. Me parece una pelea muy similar en cuanto a los tiempos de nuestra carrera: hemos debutado en Pro más o menos a la vez, él va 4-0 ahora y yo 3-0… Me gusta la pelea, me parece entretenida y es lo que quería. P. ¿Qué tipo de combate espera? Usted es muy clínico, estratégico… y Quirama ha tenido peleas caóticas. R. A ver, yo pienso que voy a hacer lo que hago siempre con mi estilo porque yo obligo a pelear ese tipo de pelea. Creo que, bueno, con todo el respeto hacia Ionescu, yo no soy Ionescu… yo no voy a entrar a ese caos de forma descontrolada. Y creo que Quirama también aprendió de eso. Yo voy a hacer mi juego, voy a pelear como peleo siempre… He visto todas sus peleas varias veces y he visto cosas que se ve que le gustan hacer en según qué momento y demás, pero bueno, este deporte es como es. Yo tengo mi game plan, eso está claro. P. ¿El objetivo es hacer carrera dentro de WOW y llegar al cinturón? R. Sí. Realmente más allá de WOW no veo necesario ir a ningún otro lado ahora mismo. Estamos en casa, WOW tiene el Fight Pass, siempre hay un gran público en los eventos, tienes los ojos de los medios encima… no me sirve de nada irme a un Cage Warriors o irme a una promotora de este estilo ahora mismo. Creo que lo tengo todo con WOW. Agradecido con la oportunidad que me han brindado esta vez, así que mi idea es hacer mínimamente los dos años que tengo de contrato con ellos… y ya espero estar en una posición para saltar. P. WOW, si no me equivoco, está ofreciendo ahora contratos de dos años como el suyo y se compromete mínimo a ofrecer tres peleas al año. R. Sí, y me gustaría hacerlas. No descartaría del todo a lo mejor pelar en diciembre, no sé, tampoco he hablado con nadie… pero no descartaría hacer otra antes de acabar el año. Luego el año que viene mínimo otras tres sí. Quiero estar activo. P. Todo el mundo quiere pelear en Valencia o Madrid… R. Valencia me gusta pero peleando en octubre noviembre no es algo inteligente, está descartado. Pero para el año que viene, buah, me encantaría la verdad. Para mí sería cumplir un sueño pelear en el Roig Arena. Vendría mucha gente de casa y es un escenario que me parece digno de cualquier plataforma de MMA. P. Hace unos meses fichó por Iridium, una agencia de representación con numerosos luchadores en UFC. ¿Qué planes tienen para usted? R. Lo de WOW es verdad que había llegado antes de hablar con Jason pero sí que le pregunté, le envié el contrato, tuvimos conversaciones y desde su punto de vista también era la mejor opción a tomar. Al final el plan está claro: desde WOW se puede ir directamente a UFC. Lo ha hecho Fabià, lo hizo Hecher, en su día Aleksandre… está claro que ahora el título de WOW tiene un peso grande, al igual que lo ha tenido en Francia promotoras como Hexagone o Ares. P. Voy a ser directo: ¿Cree que se habla poco de usted? R. A ver, yo creo que todo el mundo que sigue este deporte a nivel nacional sabe por lo menos quién soy… o en algún momento me ha visto o tiene algún pensamiento de mí. ¿Que se hable poco de mí? Pues sinceramente creo que todo el mundo está en su lugar, y si yo para que la gente hable más de mí me lo tengo que ganar a pico y pala, pues lo haré, seguiré peleando y seguiré trabajando. Creo que en la vida no se te da nada que no te mereces. Yo creo que estoy en la posición en la que tengo que estar. Tengo una frase puesta en mi biografía que es ‘vuelvete imposible de ignorar’... pero la fama no es algo que yo quiera ni necesite, ni hago esto por fama. Es verdad que esto es algo que he cambiado en mi mentalidad en los últimos dos años. Yo no quiero fama como tal, yo quiero reconocimiento por mi trabajo. Yo no hago esto para ser famoso ni porque quiera una suma de dinero, ni nada por el estilo. Hago esto porque me gusta, lo amo y es una de las cosas que me trae felicidad y paz en mi vida. Y no necesito la aprobación del resto, sinceramente. Es algo que ha cambiado. P. Me recuerda un poco a Volkanovski cuando dijo que no peleaba por títulos o legado, sino únicamente por su familia. R. Sí, ¿y quién conocía a Volkanovski cuando tenía 25 años?. La MMA es un deporte en el que pasas de desapercibido un año a otro ser el mayor prospecto. Mira Vallejos o gente así: dos años y medio, nadie lo conoce o tal... y ahora es una estrella de UFC. Así es este deporte. P. Para acabar: ¿Cómo se ve en 2027? R. Pues me veo saliendo victorioso ahora el 24 de octubre. No sabría decirte si podría pelear en diciembre o no, pero también es algo que no descarto. Me gustaría irme a principio de año a Tailandia, hacer otro mes ahí de training camp porque crecí bastante y es una experiencia que me gustaría hacer cada año si Dios me lo permite… y como te he dicho, mantenerme activo: tres peleas al año en WOW.
