articles.title: Video: SteveWillDoIt Gifts Brendan Allen A Brand New Cadillac
articles.summary: Brendan Allen had a great night at UFC Vegas 122 a couple weeks ago, and it’s still getting better. In the main event, Allen took on Christian Leroy Duncan a...
articles.body:
Brendan Allen had a great night at UFC Vegas 122 a couple weeks ago, and it's still getting better.

In the main event, Allen took on Christian Leroy Duncan and held off the Englishman's rise in a bloody five-round scrap. In the very last round of their competitive battle, Allen was able to take his opponent's back and lock in the submission (watch here) , securing an extra $100k bonus as a result of his late finish. As it turns out, that would not be Allen's only bonus stemming from the evening!

Social media star SteveWillDoIt loves to throw money around and is a supporter of "All In." After Allen's big win, SteveWillDoIt (real name Stephen Deleonardis) paid for a brand new Cadillac for the surging 185-pound contender. "Congrats to my fighter Brandan Allen," Deleonardis wrote on X . "This mother f—ker just got a caddilac as a performance bonus!!!!"

If the nearly $190k wire transfer wasn't proof enough, Allen posted a video showing off his new wheels still in the dealership and thanking SteveWillDoIt and his associated companies/sponsors.

"We're here at Cadillac New Orleans," Allen said. "There that fight bonus from your boy SteveWillDoIt … this is f—king insane. Absolutely gorgeous man."

After the big win, Allen has won four straight bouts and successfully reasserted himself into the Middleweight title mix. He's been gunning for a grudge match versus former champion Dricus du Plessis for years now , and perhaps the timing is finally right. Either way, Allen should find himself in a title eliminator bout sooner rather than later, and he has a fancy new car to get him safely to the gym.

articles.title: “Rumors and talk”: Islam Makhachev’s manager gives final say on rumored bout with Carlos Prates at UFC 336
articles.summary: A rumored fight between Islam Makhachev and Carlos Prates at UFC 336 in Toronto is currently far from being finalized.
articles.body: A rumored fight between Islam Makhachev and Carlos Prates at UFC 336 in Toronto is currently far from being finalized. Makhachev’s manager has played down the growing reports surrounding a possible January showdown, saying negotiations are still ongoing and nothing has been confirmed.The welterweight champion has been linked with Prates following his recent run in the UFC. However, Makhachev’s team has made it clear that fans should not treat the rumored matchup as official. The event, opponent and date are yet to be finalized, despite increasing speculation about a potential UFC 336 fight.Islam Makhachev vs Carlos Prates remains only a rumorIslam Makhachev’s manager Ali Abdelaziz addressed the speculation in comments to Russian outlet Ushatayka. He confirmed that discussions are taking place but stressed that the potential fight is nowhere near becoming official.“As of now, it’s not close to becoming a reality. It’s all just rumors and talk. Negotiations are ongoing, but confirming he’ll fight on a certain date and against a certain opponent is still far from realistic”, he said.The comments come after reports linked Makhachev with a January return at UFC 336 in Toronto. Carlos Prates has emerged as one of the names being discussed as a possible opponent.Prates has attracted significant attention during his UFC career because of his dangerous striking and rapid rise through the welterweight division. A fight against Makhachev would represent one of the biggest opportunities of his career.However, there is currently no official confirmation from the UFC that Makhachev will compete at UFC 336. There is also no confirmed agreement between the champion and Prates.Makhachev remains one of the biggest names in the UFC. The Russian fighter moved to welterweight after an outstanding run at lightweight. He previously held the UFC lightweight championship before making the move up and winning a second UFC title.His professional record stands at 29-1. He has also built an impressive winning streak inside the UFC and remains at the top of the promotion’s pound-for-pound rankings.Makhachev most recently defended his welterweight title against Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia. He earned a unanimous decision after a dominant performance in the grappling exchanges.Machado Garry had moments of success with his striking, but Makhachev’s pressure and wrestling remained decisive. The victory extended Makhachev’s UFC winning streak to 17 fights.Away from fighting, Makhachev has also taken on a new challenge. He recently enrolled as a master’s student at Plekhanov Russian University of Economics’ Dubai branch.The university praised the champion for continuing his education while competing at the highest level of MMA.For now, Makhachev’s next opponent remains uncertain. articles.title: MVP: MMA fighters should 'form a union' over pay, says Michael 'Venom' Page
articles.summary: Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport.
articles.body:
Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport.

The 39-year-old signed a deal with Misfits Boxing earlier this month after leaving the UFC.

Page, better known as MVP, won five of his six bouts in the UFC after debuting in 2024 but was critical of the money its fighters earn , compared with top-level athletes in other sports.

After joining Misfits, where Page says he will earn "a lot more" than he did in the UFC, the Briton wants to use his platform to empower fellow fighters.

Page points to the Muhammad Ali Act - a 2000 US law designed to protect boxers' rights and combat potential monopolies - as something which he'd like to replicate in MMA.

"It's less about speaking out now, it's more about forming a union and coming together. We have to move as one," Page told BBC Sport.

"If all fighters said 'we're not gonna do it', then UFC doesn't exist. That's the important thing for fighters to remember. It's not just the machine of UFC, you guys are the nuts and bolts that help the machine move.

"A fighters union is what's important - the Muhammad Ali Act is what has allowed boxers to be paid well and the same thing needs to happen in MMA."

Fighter pay has been questioned by athletes and the media this year after boxer Conor Benn signed a reported £11m one-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing.

Zuffa Boxing is owned by UFC president Dana White, so critics have asked why the 57-year-old isn't paying similar amounts to his MMA fighters under contract.

White has repeatedly defended fighter pay in the UFC, referencing the promotion's £5.7bn broadcast deal with Paramount.

Last week, after criticism from UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland , White pointed to the American signing a new contract in May.

Page says criticism like that of Strickland is "common" in the UFC, but most fighters don't speak out in case of repercussions.

"You speak to other athletes and it's a very common thing. Most people are not willing to say anything because it will affect them," said Page.

"I feel if I don't say anything, silence is going along with it and you're part of the problem. But I also understand you have your own bills to pay, so I'm not against anyone that doesn't either.

"If more people spoke out then they'd have to do something but it's difficult if we're not doing it as a unit, you can get ousted and other things can happen."

Page says he is "excited" to box in Misfits, and discussions have taken place about incorporating MMA into the promotion, but his main goal is to create a healthier financial space for the younger generation.

"The aim is to get them well paid, well looked after and well treated in the MMA space and bring competition against other shows," said Page.

"Which is good for fighters, it means they have alternative spaces to go to and they can negotiate better because of it.

"I see people in the UFC still struggling and I don't think there's another sport you can get to the top of your field and be struggling financially. I definitely want better for fighters."

Despite his criticisms of fighter pay, Page says he "for the most part loved" his time in the UFC.

He praised the promotion's staff, its Performance Institute - regarded as the gold standard among MMA training facilities - and its fans.

However, Page, who won all of his fights in the promotion by decision, faced criticism from fans over his lack of knockouts and admits he might have approached things differently in hindsight.

"I wish I could have done more with my performances, but overall I loved it," he said.

"I think the game has slightly shifted. It's not about who's the most skilled anymore, it's about guys who are willing to put themselves through hell and shave years off their life every single time they fight.

"If I was a bit more aware of that I would have shifted a little bit to try and compensate for that."

Page says he's aiming to make his debut in Misfits "in the first part of next year" but it has not been decided if it will be under boxing or MMA rules.

He mentioned former UFC stars Nate Diaz and Darren Till as interesting match-ups, but reiterated that no discussions about potential opponents have taken place yet.

articles.title: Fabio Wardley offered route back to world title after 'rest and recovery' - 'We'll see where we go. He's a dangerous man'
articles.summary: Promoter Frank Warren believes Fabio Wardley can return to world title contention if the former WBO heavyweight champion chooses to continue boxing; Wardley lost a second consecutive bout to Daniel Dubois on Saturday when the Londoner beat him in two rounds at the O2 Arena
articles.body:
Wardley was unable to regain the WBO world title after he was stopped in the second round of his second fight with Dubois at The O2 on Saturday.

But his manager Mike Ofo firmly believes that Wardley can challenge one of the other world champions after a "well-earned rest".

Ofo told Sky Sports : "Fabio has had a remarkable run, and there is no doubt that he still has a bright future ahead of him.

"Now is the time for him to enjoy a well-earned rest, to recover and consider his options. His journey has already been nothing short of remarkable, an extraordinary story of grit, determination and achievement.

"Clearly, he has never shied away from a challenge and has chosen to face the toughest opponents at every turn.

"I fully expect him to continue competing at the very highest levels of the sport and to win another world title if that is what he chooses to do."

Oleksandr Usyk's decision to vacate his world titles has opened up new opportunities as Murat Gassiev holds a WBA title, while Agit Kabayel is the WBC champion, and Filip Hrgovic holds the IBF belt.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will also fight for the WBA 'super' title in Cardiff on December 11.

Promoter Frank Warren intends to steer Wardley back into world title contention.

Asked if Wardley remains a threat to the division's top fighters, Warren told Sky Sports ' Toe 2 Toe podcast: "He's knocked over guys that have never been knocked over before.

"If he catches you, you're in trouble, and he's capable of doing that, but he's got to take a rest now and he's got to weigh up his chances and where he thinks he can go.

"I'm sure when he does come back, he'll have, as we call it in the trade, a warm-up fight. But if he does come back, he'll want to fight for a title again. He's a former world champion."

Wardley has reached the elite level of the sport, despite turning professional after a spell as a 'white-collar fighter' and Warren believes his remarkable success story can have another chapter.

"He'll be out for a while now and let him just rest and come back; if he does come back, and we'll see where we go with him," Warren said.

"You've got to look at some of the wins he's had. He beat Joe Parker, who was ranked No 1 in the world and everyone was saying, 'When is he going to get his shot at a world title?'

"They were backing Joe Parker to beat Daniel and to give Usyk a real tough fight and he beat him, he stopped him. I take my hat off to him.

"All of the things you've just mentioned, he never had a single amateur fight, learnt on the job, and look where he got himself, so he should be unbelievably proud of himself.

"He's a big puncher. You look at that knockout he had with Frazer Clarke. The first fight was a good fight but the second one he knocked him out in the first round and look what he did to Justis Huni. Massively behind against a very good boxer and he knocked him over. Even with Daniel, he had him on the floor twice in their first fight. He's a dangerous man.

"You look back over the years and I'm not saying he's Lennox Lewis, but Lennox, he lost against Hasim Rahman, he lost against Oliver McCall but down the road he avenged those defeats.

"A lot of these guys have been beaten in fights over the years and this era now, there's some really good fighters out there."

articles.summary: After months of waiting around and seeing rumors emerge, Netflix has now confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year....
articles.body:
After months of waiting around and seeing rumors emerge, Netflix has now confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year. The fight is now set to take place on Dec. 11, 2026, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

A few weeks ago, UFC president Dana White claimed to have a significant role in promoting and producing the Fury vs. Joshua fight. However, Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn publicly disagreed with White's alleged involvement. This soon followed a back-and-forth banter between the two , with the Misfits Boxing co-founder also suggesting a match between the two.

While White insists on his involvement in the fight , Hearn continues to claim that the UFC President is contractually barred from having any involvement in the Joshua vs. Fury boxing match.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Eddie Hearn has been Joshua's promoter since he made his professional debut in 2013. Joshua's contract for his fight with Fury is believed to specifically state that Dana White cannot be involved in the event.

"Under our contract, he can't. So that's really where we stand on it. Sela has confirmed to us in writing that Dana White and the UFC are not doing the production for this show. So, we have to go through the same process, blah blah blah.

"We will speak to Netflix and guess what? Whisper, the production company that did the production for Fury/Makhmudov, they have a contract to do the production for Fury vs. AJ on Netflix," Hearn said while speaking on iFL TV on YouTube.

Hearn finished by claiming that if White and the UFC want to speak with him regarding changing the contract about the production, he is open to a conversation. Despite the disagreements, the fight is still on for Dec. 2026.

articles.title: Former UFC champion explains why he's up for 'Proper' challenge
articles.summary: "The fight definitely makes sense." But does it?
articles.body:
Former UFC champion Belal Muhammad wants a "Proper" challenge.

Muhammad (24-6 MMA, 15-6 UFC) has been on a recent losing streak and sees a matchup against Mike Malott as a real possibility that could benefit both fighters. Malott (15-2-1 MMA, 8-1 UFC) is coming off a Knockout of the Year-contending finish of Joaquin Buckley in the main event of UFC Fight Night 291 on his home country's soil. Malott doesn't call out opponents directly, but others have done it for him.

"People are bringing up my name a lot, for sure," Muhammad said in a YouTube video. "The fight definitely makes sense."

Muhammad last fought at UFC Fight Night 278, where he lost a unanimous decision to Gabriel Bonfim in the main event. That result marked his third consecutive loss in a rough stretch that includes losses to former champ Jack Della Maddalena and former title challenger Ian Machado Garry . Muhammad has been wanting to face fellow former champion Kamaru Usman for some time now, but he isn't willing to sit out much longer.

"Obviously, when I'm looking at the division, I'm looking at who I want to fight," Muhammad said. "You know we want to fight Usman, but I'm not going to sit there and wait."

For Malott, a fight against Muhammad would make sense. Malott is on a five-fight winning streak, and despite Muhammad's skid, the fight represents a step up in competition. Malott has never faced a former UFC titleholder in the octagon. The closest on his resume is former title challenger Gilbert Burns.

Muhammad wants to get back to action soon, and January's UFC 336 in Toronto could be a good fit for Malott to fight again in Canada. In the latest USA TODAY Sports/MMA Junkie welterweight rankings , Muhammad holds the No. 7 spot, while Malott ranks No. 9.

"When I'm looking at who's hot right now, who's on a streak, Mike Malott got a good winning streak going," Muhammad said. "A win over him puts you in a good spot, puts you back into the mix, and reminds people who you are. So, for myself, it's one of those situations where if Usman's not trying to go, for sure, 'Proper' Mike Malott would definitely be a yes on my end. So, we'll see what the UFC does. We'll see what the UFC brings and what they want to do with it."

articles.title: Johnny Fisher will reach "another level" for next fight, says Zuffa Boxing's Dana White | Charles Martin wants Fisher fight
articles.summary: Zuffa Boxing promoter Dana White expects Johnny Fisher to reach a new level for his next fight as he invites him to use the UFC Performance Institute in Las Vegas; Fisher won a draining bout in his Zuffa debut in September; former world champion Charles Martin is open to fighting Fisher
articles.body:
Fisher had his first bout with new promoter Zuffa Boxing in September, coming through a draining 10-round battle with Michael Pirotton.

"He looked good until he started gassing out in the last couple of rounds. But he fought through it, won the fight and I'm excited to see him fight again. He's fun, the crowd is fun, his family are good, fun people and I love having him a part of Zuffa Boxing," White told Sky Sports .

Fisher is a hugely popular figure on social media, known for his love of Chinese takeout. He may though need to improve on his conditioning for his next fight. White has invited him to make use of the UFC's Performance Institute.

"I have seen something where he said he overtrained for the fight, which is a possibility. I don't know, only he knows. But he should absolutely positively come out to Las Vegas and spend some time at the PI [performance institute]," White said.

"All the fighters should. It's incredible. It's an unbelievable amenity you get being a part of our company. He should do that."

White is certainly expecting an improved Fisher in his next fight.

"He didn't look terrible. He gassed out there. But I tell you what I really liked about it, when you see a guy gas like he did and you push yourself through, you don't quit and you make it through that, it just takes you to another level for your next fight," the promoter said.

"Mentally now he knows what he did. Did he overtrain, did he not train enough? He knows and now he knows what he needs to fix coming into his next fight so it'll be exciting to see what tweaks he makes in his training for his next fight."

Fisher will have appealing options for his next fight. Dillian Whyte was ringside for his last bout at the Copper Box and former world champion Charles Martin is open to boxing Fisher.

Martin's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports : "He's had an amazing career and became IBF heavyweight champion. He wants one more big opportunity."

Martin, who lost to Anthony Joshua at the O2 in 2016, is looking to fight in Britain again next year. Borao said: "Possible opponents Johnny Fisher, Dillian Whyte or perhaps another UK fighter. We will have to see what happens but Charles is going to make one more big push."

Watch Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke on November 7 at the Copper Box Arena live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: As missiles rain down on Riyadh, WWE's Crown Jewel dilemma is becoming unavoidable
articles.summary: With millions of dollars on the line and Saudi Arabia under attack, WWE faces an increasingly difficult choice: Put its talent and staff at risk, or jeopardi...
articles.body:
It's the most intriguing boardroom storyline in pro-wrestling — and one you shouldn't expect to see in the next season of "WWE Unreal . " Should WWE go ahead with its Crown Jewel event, scheduled to take place Nov. 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, or opt for a safer alternative back in the U.S.?

That the Saudi security situation has deteriorated in the weeks after this year's Crown Jewel was first announced on Sept. 1 is an understatement. Since then, we've seen the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launch a barrage of missile attacks on Riyadh airport , claiming the lives of at least 20 people and injuring at least 370 in what is already the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade.

Right now, WWE is insisting the show will go ahead — a decision that flies in the face of what other businesses and sports events are doing. Just this week, we've seen a bunch of major events in Riyadh postponed, including Saudi Arabia's annual Davos in the Desert, as well as the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and Saudi International golf tournament.

Why is WWE plowing ahead with Crown Jewel when others are playing it safe? As ever, money talks. Anyone who has spent five minutes following TKO's financials knows how important the Saudis are for WWE — in recent years, they've contributed around one quarter of the company's live-event revenues. The average Saudi show brings in more money than this year's WrestleMania.

Forgoing that reported $50 million fee for Crown Jewel might be one thing. But the tougher question is what it might mean for the future relationship with the Saudis, particularly when the Kingdom is looking to ramp up its investment in WWE in order to bring WrestleMania to Riyadh next year.

We don't know exactly how much Saudi Arabia is shelling out for 'Mania 43, though the estimates of $150 million would appear credible. If anything, they could be said to be a little conservative, given that WrestleMania is at least three times bigger than the typical WWE PLE. What is certain, though, is that this will be the largest payment yet for WWE.

All of which brings us to Turki Alalshikh, the man who controls the Saudi purse strings. Perhaps the most intriguing twist in this whole Crown Jewel saga is the reports that WWE insiders are worried Alalshikh's glazing of Saul "Canelo" Alvarez — who is set to fight in Riyadh on Oct. 31 — on social media is a preemptive dig at those in TKO towers.

How so? When "Canelo" confirmed he would be going through with the fight, Alalshikh posted "hard times reveal true friends." One way to read that is a coded warning that those who cancel their commitments aren't true friends of Turki Alalshikh — and that's always a dangerous position to be in. Not just in the world of combat sports.

Would the country really pull the plug on SaudiMania if WWE canceled Crown Jewel? All common sense would suggest not. But that's the problem with relying on one source for such a hefty chunk of your revenue — you can't really afford to call their bluff. On the other hand, it's not like the other course of action is safe either, with the risk of missiles raining down on Riyadh airport. So what's a TKO executive to do?

If it's so dangerous, you might ask, why is "Canelo" fighting there on Halloween? Well, you'd probably have to ask him. Which is sort of the point: "Canelo" is one man who can make his own decision whether to go to Riyadh to collect his purse or not. (He's also a man who gets punched for a living, so he probably has a different outlook on risk than your typical Wall Street suit.)

More seriously, "Canelo" isn't a corporate entity like TKO. He doesn't have to take a whole production crew, or send dozens of supporting talent on commercial jets into Riyadh airport. He doesn't have to justify the fallout to shareholders should the proverbial mess really hit the fan. He's never going to be dragged in front of Congress like the bosses of Enron and Facebook when they faced scandals.

So given all that, will WWE go through with the show? Without knowing what's in Nick Khan's head, it's hard to do much more than speculate at this point. Obviously one thing that could influence the decision is how the security situation holds up over the next few weeks. Right now, it's been over a week since the last attack on Riyadh, but fighting continues in Yemen.

According to credible media reports, WWE does at least have a backup venue in the States if they need it. Though that's still going to leave an alleged $50 million hole in the next earnings report and a bunch of awkward questions about WrestleMania 43. Even a single emoji from Alalshikh's social media profile could hammer the TKO stock price.

In that situation, I don't doubt they could weather the storm in the long run. But the more pertinent question would be, why they didn't see the dark clouds on the horizon beforehand? If you're going to jump into bed with an absolute monarchy in one of the world's most unstable regions, can you really be surprised when things get sticky?

That's the main problem here: WWE might be between a rock and a hard place with Crown Jewel, but you can't say they weren't the ones who walked into that situation in the first place. Can they get themselves out of it without triggering a bigger headache down the line? Over to you, Nick Khan.

articles.summary: La compañía de MMA líder a nivel nacional regresa al País Vasco con una cartelera apasionante
articles.body: Este sábado 24 de octubre, WOW FC regresa a Vitoria para celebrar WOW 33. Como cada año, el Buesa Arena se vestirá de gala para celebrar uno de los grandes eventos del año, cuyo combate estelar será el que enfrente a Borja García (7-2) y Ander Sánchez (3-3) por el 'Trono del Norte'. Una pelea entre dos de los nombres más mediáticos de nuestro país que no dejará indiferente a nadie, y que será sinónimo de acción asegurada. Además, como ya pasó en Sevilla, la cartelera se podrá seguir en directo por el canal de Cristiano Ronaldo y a través de MARCA.com de manera gratuita. Más allá del combate entre Borja y Ander, también hay que destacar la presencia de otros nombres importantes para la empresa. Tras sumar dos derrotas consecutivas, Yaman 'El Diamante' (3-2) regresa a su tierra para medirse a Ubay González (4-3), mientras que Delffy Humer (3-0), último verdugo de Yaman, se enfrentará a Joao Lucas Rocha (4-2) para meterse de lleno en la pelea por el cinturón vacante de peso mosca. Otro héroe local como Arkaitz 'Gudari' Ramos (9-7) se medirá a Jeferson Costa (5-3) en el combate estelar para ser profeta en su tierra, y Daniel Richardson (3-0) se enfrentará a Willmar Quirama (4-0-1) en lo que promete ser uno de los grandes duelos de la noche. En total habrá 13 combates que harán las delicias del respetable, y que se podrán seguir de manera gratuita. El evento dará comienzo a las 17:30h de este sábado 24 de octubre, y se podrá seguir a través del canal de Youtube de Cristiano Ronaldo y MARCA.com de forma gratuita. Además, a nivel global también se podrá seguir por UFC Fight Pass como viene siendo habitual. articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights After WrestleDream 2026
articles.summary: Following an action-packed WrestleDream, the October 21 edition of Dynamite from the Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida promised a massive debut and dramatic fallout.
articles.body:
Following an action-packed WrestleDream, the October 21 edition of Dynamite from the Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida promised a massive debut and dramatic fallout.

Ilja Dragunov competed for the first time in an All Elite Wrestling ring against "Speedball" Mike Bailey. Will Ospreay teamed with Adam Copeland against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight.

Queen Aminata and a returning Maya World competed for the next shot at Persephone's TBS Championship. The Young Bucks fought the Don Callis Family's Mark Davis and Jake Doyle in Championship Eliminator action.

For all the results, highlights and live grades from Dynamite, keep scrolling down.

World Tag Team Championships Eliminator: Young Bucks vs. Mark Davis and Jake Doyle

Last Time in Action: Matt and Nick Jackson defeated Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher to retain the World Tag Team Championships (WrestleDream, October 17); Mark Davis and Jake Doyle alongside Wardlow defeated The Death Riders (Dynamite, October 14).

Davis and Doyle went right after The Young Bucks to start the match, dragging them outside and throwing them around.

Doyle Powerbombed Nick through the timekeeper's table. Davis laid into Matt with a trio of Close Your Eyes Piledrivers while Doyle knocked out Nick with a Bearhug. The two then pinned both champions together.

This was a genuinely shocking opener for the usual AEW standard. Typically, AEW uses the opener for a longer action-packed contest to heat up the crowd.

Instead, Davis and Doyle absolutely dominated, taking advantage of the damage Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher did to the champions on Saturday.

The big men of the Don Callis Family needed a big heat-up moment, and this was good as it gets. The Young Bucks have a monumental hill to climb when their titles are on the line.

This also helped continue to sell that Davis is one of the scariest big men in AEW right now for anyone to run into.

While more segment than true match, this was a rousing success in immediately heating up credible threats to the World Tag Team Championships.

Davis and Doyle def. Matt and Nick by pinfall to earn a future World Tag Team Championships match.

On commentary, Callis sold that Davis and Doyle knew The Young Bucks were hurting after WrestleDream, which played out quickly.

Excalibur transitioned to a montage recap for WrestleDream after the match, selling this was earlier than they expected to play the video.

Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland vs. Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher

Last Time in Action: Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher lost to The Young Bucks (WrestleDream, October 17). This is the first time Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland have teamed, but they faced off at WrestleDream in the Clockwork Carnage match won by Ospreay.

While Ospreay and Cope worked well together to start, the athleticism of Knight and Fletcher caused problems for the new team.

The Protostar took down The Aerial Assassin with a combination Powerbomb/Dropkick with The Jet into the commercial break.

The Don Callis Family managed to isolated Ospreay through the break, who finally broke his way free with a Springboard Forearm Smash on Knight.

Cope got the hot tag and rolled over Knight with a Pop-Up Facebuster. He teased a Spear, but The Jet rolled outside. Fletcher took out The Rated-R Superstar with a Superkick into a Knight Crossbody for a near-fall.

The Aerial Assassin rallied The Rated-R Superstar, but Fletcher took him out with an Enzuigiri. Kazuchika Okada then arrived to distract Cope and Ospreay.

The Rated-R Superstar caught Fletcher with a Killswitch and a Spear to Knight, but Okada blasted Cope with the International Championship into a Fletcher Brainbuster for the victory.

Afterward, The Don Callis Family attacked Cope and Ospreay until Darby Allin arrived. He revealed that Steven Borden was back, and they stormed the ring with Nick Jackson and weapons to clear out The Family.

Borden then declared he was back and wanted The Family in Blood & Guts.

AEW doubled down on the dangers of The Callis Family, giving them another big victory. This was less definitive but nonetheless effective in selling that this group could beat anyone right now.

Cope and Ospreay did not show much chemistry, but that made sense given their unfamiliarity with one another. It was the right choice for the experienced team to win.

The Blood & Guts match will be good, but AEW definitely had better built feuds for the cage. Instead, it looks like the goal is to get big names in the cage, particularly Ospreay and Cope.

Borden and Allin have the most personal reason to fight The Family, and hopefully they will be the emotional focus of the build.

Fletcher and Knight def. Cope and Ospreay by pinfall.

Cope made clear to Callis, who remained on commentary, that he hated him.

Okada hid from the referee after bloodying Cope but immediately popped into the ring once the bell rang to keep attacking.

Callis gave the Men's World Championship to Fletcher, teasing he could be the next challenger for The Aerial Assassin.

Borden coming back from injury right into Blood & Guts is a good sign that he is back fully healthy... or just crazy.

Last Time in Action: Swerve Strickland alongside New Level lost to The Good, The Bad, and El Guapo (WrestleDream, October 17); Tome Philip alongside Gino Medina and Nic Nolan lost to The Don Callis Family (Collision, July 18).

Swerve came in angry and took out Filip with a House Call and Vertebreaker for a quick victory.

Not much to say for this one as it was just a stat padder for The Mogul. He sold his anger and annoyance about WrestleDream and leaves with a win.

Since there was no follow-up yet with Kofi and Austin Creed, it is unclear if this means Swerve is going back to singles action fully just yet.

Swerve barely got his jacket off for the match, and Prince Nana helped him put it right back on afterward.

Report reveals list of next NFL international locations

Orange Cassidy and "Switchblade" Jay White vs. Daniel Garcia and Wheeler Yuta

Last Time in Action: Daniel Garcia and Wheeler Yuta alongside The Death Riders and The Dogs defeated Orange Cassidy and "Switchblade" Jay White alongside The Conglomeration and The Bang Bang Gang (WrestleDream: Tailgate Brawl, October 17).

Switchblade was a focused determined killer in the ring against Garcia and Yuta while Cassidy found a harder time early to deal with the technical offense of The Death Riders.

Yuta managed to trap Cassidy in the ring apron then take out White with a Tope Suicida into the commercial break.

Garcia caught White in the Dragon Tamer, but Cassidy made the save. Switchblade almost laid out Yuta with the Blade Runner, only for Garcia to save him.

Freshly Squeezed and Switchblade combined for an Orange Punch into a Switchblade on Yuta to seal the victory.

Four talented men competed in a fine tag match that would have fit more naturally on Collision, but AEW might be a bit low on top names following a physical WrestleDream.

It never felt like Garcia and Yuta had a chance to win despite holding a victory from the Tailgate Brawl.

The big positive was to see Switchblade worked fast and physical after his recent injury. Hopefully this is a sign that he is back to full pace.

White and Cassidy def. Garcia and Yuta by pinfall.

Excalibur announced both world tag title matches for Full Gear were official: The Brawling Birds vs. Wrathlander and The Young Bucks vs. Davis and Doyle.

Backstage, Swerve Strickland interrupted an interview with World trios champions Hangman Adam Page, Brody King, and Bandido to ask for his rematch with New Day. Hangman agreed, but Swerve wanted Texas Death. Hangman declined.

Marina Shafir Challenges Mercedes Moné/Championship Eliminator: Jon Moxley vs. Roderick Strong

Last Time in Action: Jon Moxley defeated Mark Davis to retain the Continental Championship; Roderick Strong lost alongside The Conglomeration and Bang Bang Gang to The Death Riders and The Dogs (WrestleDream, October 17).

Mercedes Moné quickly ushered Renee Paquette out of the ring during her scheduled in-ring interview and questioned who was next to fight her.

Mox's music hit as Marina Shafir marched to the ring and questioned if The CEO was scared. The champion backed down as Strong headed to the ring for his Continental Championship Eliminator.

Mox started slow against Strong, who came at him aggressively. He sent him back first into the apron to send the match to commercial break.

The strikes to the gut and back of the Continental champion continued, but Mox began to fire back with Clotheslines and punches.

Mox tripped up Strong into a Rear Naked Choke, and Strong realized he couldn't escape and tapped out.

Afterward, David Finlay and Clark Connors attacked Strong until Mox told them to back off. The Dogs turned on Mox, beating him down. They took out Gabe Kidd when he tried to stop them.

When The Death Riders and The Conglomeration arrived, White shockingly laid out Orange Cassidy. The Bang Bang Gang and Dogs worked together and laid out everyone.

Moné vs. Shafir is an intriguing match as this is the biggest opportunity The Problem has had in her wrestling career.

The two looked great together last month in trios action, and The CEO has shown she elevates everyone in the ring. However, it will be a unique physical battle for Moné, especially if they get time at Full Gear.

Mox vs. Strong was a decent match, though the Continental champion heavily sold how worn down he was, leading to a slow battle throughout.

The result did not make The Messiah of the Backbreaker look all that dangerous, but it did seem to further fuel his frustration, which could let him eventually turn heel and heat back up.

That said, the heel turn of the night was White. The tag match from earlier looks even less necessary after this, but this was an incredible post-match angle.

The Dogs vs. Bang Bang Gang feud was losing steam, and this immediately gave it a fresh path forward. This unofficial Bullet Club reunion might be exactly what everyone needed.

Switchblade as the heel leader of a dangerous stable including multiple men playing heel for the first time in AEW is intriguing.

Finlay and Connors falling in line with White is the biggest question left to answer, but it is definitely better than them playing nice with Mox, who was already leaning face as it was.

This should allow The Death Riders to play full faces going forward. The fans want to cheer them, so there was no reason to hold back on this any longer.

The main fault with all this is that AEW announced Blood & Guts only to deliver a far more interesting stable warfare battle 30 minutes later that would have fit the cage better.

B (for the potential of Moné vs. Shafir)/C+ (for the match)/A+ (for the post-match)

Moné went off on Strong as he headed to the ring. One would assume she told him to handle his wife.

Mox caught Strong with a Cutter off a Jumping Knee attempt that almost looked RKO-esque with the fluidity.

Claudio Castagnoli looked like he was almost going to take down The Bang Bang Gang and Dogs all on his own, but the numbers game eventually became too much.

Switchblade mostly stayed out of the action but made a point to lay out Cassidy to start and Mox to finish it.

Jericho Apologizes to Nick Wayne and Tells Him He Can Be Great

Nick Wayne sauntered to the ring and mocked Jericho, calling out his double win for Y2J with many pyro explosions.

He questioned if Jericho would even show up, only to be interrupted by massive pyro as Y2J arrived.

After some annoying goading by Wayne, Jericho did apologize to The Prodigy. While he called Wayne a douchebag, he also admitted that Wayne could be one of the all-time greats.

This feels like a segment that Jericho wanted to be an all-time great moment for Wayne. Instead, it was an imperfect segment that was good enough for what it was trying to accomplish.

The Prodigy played his role well, emulating a young Jericho to the point of being actively annoying.

It was Jericho that did not quite land with his over-the-top yelling to sell that he cared about where Wayne's career could go.

Still, at the end of all this, The Prodigy is more of a star than he has ever been, and AEW did not force another match out of this feud. That is a win.

Wayne arrived to the arena in a white limo and unveiled his new shirt declaring his victory over Jericho.

As good as The Prodigy's pyro bit is, it might be too much of a crowd pleaser for a man that is going to run as a heel for a while. The crowd kept calling for more.

No. 1 Contender for TBS Championship: Maya World vs. Queen Aminata

Last Time in Action: Queen Aminata as well as Hyan and Dani Luna lost to Persephone for the TBS Championship (WrestleDream, October 17); Maya World alongside Hyan and Thunder Rose lost to Persephone, Dr. Britt Baker, DMD and Hikaru Shida (Dynamite, September 9).

This match started physical as both threw knees early. Aminata nearly caught Maya with a strong knee strike to win before the commercial break.

Back from break, Maya fired back, and the two exchanged pin attempts. Aminata tried to hit Off with Her Head, but Maya rolled outside.

Aminata set her up on a steel chair and blasted her with a vicious Missile Dropkick.

Back in the ring, The Queen knocked down Maya with the Queen's Crown followed by Off With Her Head for the victory.

Afterward, Persephone and Baker threatened Aminata, but Maya and Hyan backed up the new No. 1 contender.

This was the best match of the night up to this point as both women hit hard and moved fast to keep this crowd fully invested in this contender action.

Maya and Aminata have chemistry to spare that played well to the fans. Maya looked good in her return, but it was especially clear that Aminata was working on a higher level for a big opportunity.

Of all the challengers Persephone has had so far, this feels the most like a potential title change is in order.

It makes little sense that Aminata has never held gold in AEW, and this would be a great time to change that.

Aminata def. World by pinfall to earn a TBS Championship match next week on Fright Night Dynamite.

Persephone and Baker joined commentary to question why the TBS champion needed to face either woman she has already beaten.

While both are technically faces, Aminata took the aggressor role in this one, leaning heel.

Divine Dominion and The Triangle of Madness attacked The Brawling Birds and Wrathlander backstage, likely setting up a women's Blood and Guts match.

Ilja Dragunov vs. "Speedball" Mike Bailey

Last Time in Action: "Speedball" Mike Bailey fell short in the Clockwork Carnage match, won by Will Ospreay (WrestleDream, October 17). This was the debut of Ilja Dragunov in AEW whose last match before this was a loss in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal (SmackDown, April 17).

Speedball tried to avoid the aggressive offense of Dragunov early, taking a few physical chops but catching him with a Moonsault to the floor.

The Mad Dragon ducked a kick of Bailey that send his foot into the steel steps and followed up with a German Suplex on the floor into the final commercial break.

The two kept delivering vicious shots including a strong Senton by Dragunov and a Double Knee Drop from Speedball to Dragunov on the apron.

Bailey blocked a D-Bomb attempt with a kick and tied up his limbs in a tied straitjacket pin for a near-fall.

Speedball caught Dragunov with Time Adventure, but Dragunov tripped him off the top rope. He followed up with a Powerbomb into a D-Bomb to the leg followed by a D-Bomb to the head for the victory.

As an introduction for Dragunov to a fresh audience, this could not have gone better.

He and Speedball looked great together, and they built the physicality over the course of the match rather than going overboard early.

While it was a strike exchange, the focus of both men was heavily technical. The Mad Dragon was wearing down Speedball by going after his legs throughout.

The way both men hit each other and laid in their submission attempts looked consistently painful. They wanted this to feel as real as it could.

On a night where the action was less than AEW's best overall, Dragunov put on the most AEW-coded performance of anyone, selling why he is a perfect fit in this new environment.

While AEW sometimes has new stars come in and lose, Dragunov should look like a top threat immediately on this roster and should be treated that way.

Let Dragunov stay undefeated until the Continental Classic where he could be a real threat to win it all.

The crowd immediately knew the assignment in cheering on Dragunov as well as plenty of dueling chants for both men.

Backstage, The Don Callis Family officially accepted the challenge for Blood & Guts while promising The Family were coming for all the gold.

Samoa Joe promised he was still going back for the world title. "Jungle" Jack Perry challenged him to a rematch. Joe promised to eventually accept.

AEW aired a hype video for the FTR vs. Motor City Machine Guns Best of 5 series, announcing the next two matches for Collision then Fright Night Dynamite.

Excalibur also confirmed Swerve Strickland would be back in action on Collision against Myron Reed.

This was one of the weaker Dynamites in a while in terms of pure in-ring action, but it was one of the most eventful in terms of story build.

While it feels like the build to Blood & Guts and Full Gear could use a bit more time, AEW made the most of this show to sell some big matches to come.

This was a pure hype show from The Don Callis Family's emphatic destruction of their rivals to The Bang Bang Gang heel turn to Ilja Dragunov's memorable debut.

The way this played out, it feels clear that the company has a strong plan building for the next month, and the talent are behind building those stories.

Even with a limited roster coming off WrestleDream, this show sold that the road to Full Gear is going to be a can't-miss spectacle.

articles.title: Floyd Mayweather vs. Ryan Garcia Title Fight Announced, Details Revealed in New Social Media Post
articles.summary: Amid rumors of a potential fight, Ryan Garcia said he's set to go up against Floyd Mayweather.
articles.body:
Amid rumors of a potential fight, Ryan Garcia said he's set to go up against Floyd Mayweather.

"Trust me at first I thought this was bull***," Garcia wrote on social media. "But it's real. Floyd and I agree to a fight 147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world. 50-0 vs The current champ."

Report reveals list of next NFL international locations

Garcia also shared a photo of him and Mayweather FaceTiming.

Garcia provided more details about the fight on his Instagram .

"Just got off the phone with (Mayweather)," he said. "Talking about fighting - it's real and he wants to do a real fight 147. He and I both agreed to post this! Let's Rumble. This will be for the 147 WBC world championship I made that very clear and Floyd and I agreed to fight."

According to Uncrowned's Darshan Desai , there have been "no serious negotiations" about the fight yet, but it seems the two have at least made a verbal agreement.

Talks of a potential fight began earlier this month, when Garcia confirmed it was in the works.

Garcia clarified from the jump that he wasn't willing to fight Mayweather in an exhibition.

"And no I wouldn't do an exhibition I want his 0 on the f--king line," he wrote on social media. "How much does he actually think he got left. I'm ready Floyd, remember you made this call. I'm just returning the favor. Offer is on the table. Accept or not, if not I move foward as I have been."

Mayweather has not commented publicly on the fight.

The 49-year-old Mayweather is 50-0 in his career with 27 knockouts, but hasn't fought professionally since 2017, when he defeated Conor McGregor via knockout.

Garcia, meanwhile, is 28 years old and in the prime of his career, recording a 26-2 record with 21 knockouts. He's coming off back-to-back wins, beating Mario Barrios in February via unanimous decision for the WBC welterweight title and Conor Benn last month via knockout.

Given the massive age gap, Garcia would surely be the favorite against Mayweather.

articles.title: Yaman Mjahed: "He vuelto a reconstruirme hasta sentirme más fuerte que antes"
articles.standfirst: El peleador de Mondragón se sincera en MARCA antes de WOW 33 Vitoria
articles.summary: El peleador de Mondragón se sincera en MARCA antes de WOW 33 Vitoria
articles.body: Un año después, Yaman ‘El Diamante’ Mjahed (3-2) vuelve a pelear en WOW FC. Precisamente, en la arena en la que sufrió su última derrota: el Buesa Arena, en Vitoria. El peleador vasco se medirá a Ubay González (4-3) mientras busca recuperar el ‘aura’ perdida y volver a colocarse como una de las grandes estrellas de la compañía. En la previa, atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. Casi un año después, vuelve a la jaula de WOW… y en el sitio donde lo dejó: Vitoria. Respuesta. Gracias a Dios, soy un luchador joven, podía permitirme ese parón para... reagruparme conmigo mismo, tomar ciertas decisiones, calmar un poco las aguas, ¿no?. Como suelen decir, dar un paso atrás para dar cinco hacia adelante, ver un poco las cartas que tenía, por dónde podía tirar, y cuál era el movimiento más inteligente. Y creo que ese parón era algo necesario. Entonces, sí, así lo hice, y gracias a Dios, pues puedo volver al lugar donde lo dejé todo, que es en Vitoria. Así que, en lo personal, me gusta volver a pelear allí, en mi casa, para poder quitarme esa espinita y regalarle la victoria a mi gente, que lo sufrió la última vez. Así que, sí, es como volver a empezar... volver a continuar el libro por la página que lo habías dejado. Me siento muy feliz por eso. P. Ya tuvo una grave lesión que le obligó a parar mucho tiempo. Ahora, otro año fuera. ¿Ha sido duro? R. Siento que, al fin y al cabo, las cicatrices hacen al hombre. Las circunstancias, las adversidades muchas veces revelan el tipo de persona que es cada uno. Si eres un cobarde, lo vas a demostrar en la adversidad. Si te hundes a la mínima que algo se pone difícil, lo vas a demostrar en la adversidad. Y si realmente eres una persona fuerte, que sigue adelante y que nunca se rinde, también lo vas a demostrar en la adversidad. Así que, básicamente, estas circunstancias que me ha tocado vivir en mi vida me han demostrado a mí mismo un poco de la pasta de la que estoy hecho. Cuánto realmente estoy dispuesto a dar por hacer mi sueño realidad. Yo lo dejé todo siendo muy joven para hacer mi sueño realidad: ser luchador profesional de MMA y ser campeón del mundo algún día. Y cuando he tenido esos tropiezos, me he demostrado que esa decisión que tomé en su momento la tomé de una forma sólida. Que no fue un niño con un sueño caprichoso, sino que era un pequeño hombrecito que decidió apostar toda su vida por una misión, y que seguimos en ello. Y no tengo duda de que no será ni la segunda ni la última y que habrán muchas más caídas… pero, como suelo decirme a mí mismo, las mismas armas que me han ayudado a enfrentar las circunstancias del pasado son las que me van a ayudar a afrontar las circunstancias del futuro. Entonces, por esa parte, dadas todas las adversidades, venga lo que venga, estoy tranquilo porque me he demostrado a mí mismo una y otra vez que tengo lo suficiente para levantarme una y mil veces. P. ¿Hubo momentos de duda? R. Estuve a punto de rendirme. Yo el día que terminé el combate en Vitoria y creo que eres la primera persona a la primera persona que se lo digo respecto a medios y prensa… yo dije, ‘yo no vuelvo a pisar una jaula’. Te lo digo en serio. Mi primer pensamiento fue: ‘yo no voy a volver a pasar todo el proceso de prepararme, todo el proceso de lo que conlleva un combate’. Decía, ‘¿para qué? ¿para esto?’. Y recuerdo que cuando bajé las escaleras de Vitoria, inconscientemente empecé a pedir perdón a la gente. No sé por qué. Yo creo que fue una forma inconsciente. Como diciendo, ‘me he rendido’, ¿sabes?. Y ese sentimiento me duró tiempo… Me costó. La verdad que fue un golpe, fue un golpe duro. Yo diría que el más duro hasta el momento. No por la derrota en sí, sino por todo lo que conllevaba la anterior pelea también. Entonces fue un momento bastante, bastante duro. Pero como te he dicho al principio, las circunstancias revelan al hombre. Y yo no me sentía bien conmigo mismo porque no era el lugar donde quería estar. Yo, algo dentro de mí, una voz dentro de mí siempre me decía que yo no estoy destinado a vivir en un estado así. Entonces dejé de luchar contra ello, lo acepté, tomé las decisiones que tenía que tomar, hice lo que tenía que hacer y empecé a reconstruirme poco a poco hasta el punto de ahora en el que me siento, gracias a Dios, más fuerte que antes. Y creo que realmente eso es lo que determina unos atletas de otros, unos luchadores de otros, o unas personas de otras. Pero sí, fue muy duro. Fue muy, muy, muy duro. P. Pero al final, si se ponen en perspectiva sus derrotas, son ante un Hecher Sosa que ahora está en UFC y ante un Delffy Humer que está invicto… R. En esas noches oscuras también empiezas a pensar y darle vueltas a la cabeza y decir, a ver, ‘¿pero qué ha pasado? ¿por qué ha pasado?’. También llego a esos pensamientos. ‘Bueno, a ver, los tropiezos que he tenido han sido contra gente que no ha sido contra el vecino de mi barrio, ¿no?’. También digo, ‘¿cuántas peleas he tenido en WOW?’. Contando mi carrera profesional y amateur, he sido el luchador creo que con el récord de más finalizaciones dentro de la empresa y más victorias dentro de la empresa consecutivamente y, de repente, me han llegado dos tropiezos seguidos. Pero eso no tacha de la lista todo el listado que he tenido de victorias consecutivas, una detrás de otra durante casi cuatro años. Entonces, llegas a esas conclusiones, sientes que no estás en el lugar que quieres estar y empiezas a reconstruirte. Yo creo que es parte del proceso, y no solamente como atleta, también en el día a día de una persona. Cualquier persona de a pie de la calle tiene este tipo de adversidades, esos momentos en los que son como esos puntos canon de tu vida en los que te hacen reflexionar, tomar decisiones. Y, si lo haces bien, siempre son para algo bueno y para algo positivo en el futuro. P. ¿Qué diría que es lo más importante que ha sacado de este proceso de casi un año? R. Te lo resumiré en una frase: creemos que no tener miedo a la muerte nos hace fuertes, pero realmente nos hace débiles. ¿Me entiendes?. Es decir, muchas veces creemos que no tener miedo es la salvación para todo y muchas veces tener miedo es lo único que te salva. Aferrarte a la vida es lo único que te salva. No luchamos porque no tengamos miedo a morir, luchamos porque amamos la vida. Entonces yo creo que ese ha sido el aprendizaje de este año. He luchado porque amo mi sueño, he luchado porque amo vivir estas experiencias, sean buenas o sean malas. P. Hablemos del futuro. Lleva unas semanas en Marbella preparando esta pelea en WOW 33 Vitoria. ¿Por qué ese cambio? R. Este año ha sido un año de aprendizaje individual conmigo mismo y en lo colectivo. Me he movido un montón, he viajado, he salido de España, he tratado de volver a ese punto cero, a esos días de amateur, por así decirlo, en los que no conocía nada del deporte y quería aprender y nutrirme de todo el mundo. ¿Por qué no? Yo recuerdo una frase que decía Conor McGregor: ‘el día que dejas de aprender es el día que te preparas para perder’. Y yo me di cuenta en cierto momento que quizá me había acomodado demasiado en mi casa. Tengo un equipo maravilloso, tengo un entrenador, Javi, increíble, unos compañeros espectaculares… pero creo que muchas veces exponernos a la incertidumbre de un lugar ajeno, creo que enriquece mucho a un atleta y más a un atleta que se dedica a pelear. Porque te adaptas a sentirte cómodo en un lugar extraño, y realmente eso es lo que te vas a encontrar en la jaula. Entonces he tratado de exponerme mucho. He entrenado con todo tipo de luchadores, me he movido con luchadores de UFC, con luchadores de PFL, luchadores de todo tipo, con amigos, con gente conocida… y he ido a exponerme olvidando cualquier tipo de atadura conmigo mismo, no queriendo demostrar nada, yendo a tumba abierta a aprender, a absorber y enriquecerme. Y eso es lo que he hecho todo este año. Y luego la última fase de mi camp pues sí que la he trasladado aquí a Marbella, con el coach Gabriel, un entrenador maravilloso. No es muy conocido aquí en el panorama nacional, él es italiano, pero me está ayudando un montón, junto a mis compañeros también. Así que sí, estamos haciendo un gran trabajo, me estoy sintiendo muy bien, lo estoy disfrutando, hay buen tiempo, buenos compañeros, buena energía, y eso es todo lo que necesita un atleta para salir adelante. P. ¿Qué versión de Yaman puede esperar la gente en Vitoria? R. Yaman es lo que es. Va cambiando de formas, va evolucionando, pero la esencia nunca se pierde… Entonces, vamos a ver a un Yaman muy sereno, muy tranquilo, y que no pretende nada, que no busca nada, que no quiere forzar nada, que quiere que todo venga. No va a ir a buscar un KO, no va a ir a buscar una finalización, va a dejar que todo llegue a su debido momento. No malinterpretes mis palabras, no malinterpretes ni confundas mi serenidad con debilidad. Pienso entrar ahí preparado, afilado, peligroso, venenoso, buscando circunstancias y momentos de peligro en todo momento. Listo para todo y dispuesto a todo. Eso es lo que te puedo decir. P. Supongo que un reto personal es buscar la condición de ser una de las caras de WOW. R. Es verdad. Era la cara visible de WOW durante años. El último contendiente al título de 61 kilos he sido yo. Los datos están ahí, pero mi trabajo está aquí. Y ahora es momento de unificar todo. Y el día 24, si Dios quiere, será el día. No tengo prisa. Yo sé que todo llegará. Estoy en esa llanura del potencial latente. He trabajado mucho, me he ganado mi lugar con sangre, sudor y lágrimas. Solamente necesito ese último ‘boom’ para que todo vuelva a florecer. Así que sin prisa. Todo llegará con calma. P. Vuelve al peso gallo. ¿Lo de pelear en el mosca fue un error? R. Vuelvo a mi categoría. Y también este año ha sido un momento de ser sincero conmigo mismo y realmente creo que bajar al peso mosca fue un error. Yo de por sí soy un 61 kilos muy grande. Lo que pasa es que soy joven. Gracias a Dios tengo una muy buena genética y di 57 kilos de una forma relativamente fácil. Pero sufrida, obviamente. Estuve un montón de meses a dieta para poder dar ese peso bien. Pero el momento de la rehidratación no fue bien y no me sentí bien en el combate. Y no es normal que un jab me noquee. Entonces, sin desmeritar a Delffy, que es un luchador increíble y tiene una mano que le pesa… pero un jab me noqueó. Y eso no es normal. Entonces me reuní con mi equipo y decidimos que esa categoría no era la adecuada por todo el sacrificio que conllevaba. Por lo duro que fue y porque no me encontraba en un estado físico óptimo. No tenía mi velocidad, mi explosividad, mi reactividad, mi fluidez… todo eso se fue. Y eso que hice un gran campamento. Así que la decisión correcta era volver a 61 kilos, que es donde he hecho toda mi carrera, donde me he sentido muy bien, donde he dominado siempre. Así que volvemos a ese peso y el tiempo hará el resto.

articles.title: Jon Jones consideraba a Ilia Topuria la "primera amenaza" para su puesto de GOAT de las MMA
articles.standfirst: Así opinaba el estadounidense antes de la derrota del 'Matador' ante Gaethje
articles.summary: Así opinaba el estadounidense antes de la derrota del 'Matador' ante Gaethje
articles.body: De forma casi unánime, Jon Jones es considerado el GOAT de las MMA. Una carrera brillante en el peso semipesado (ocho defensas del título) y campeón del peso pesado, solamente suma una derrota en su carrera por las 28 victorias logradas... y fue por descalificación tras unos codazos que ahora, en 2026, son válidos según reglamentación. Un estatus, el del GOAT de las MMA, que el estadounidense solamente veía "amenazado" por Ilia Topuria. El hispanogeorgiano, campeón en el peso pluma y el ligero, llegaba invicto a UFC Casa Blanca en busca de su victoria número 18 y consolidar su reinado en la división de las 155 libras. Pero perdió. “Ilia Topuria me entusiasma”, dijo Jones en una entrevista con Prince Street Pizza. “Antes de esa velada en la Casa Blanca, lo consideraba invencible. Por mucho que desee que otros peleadores vengan, superen mis récords y se conviertan en los mejores, hay otra parte de mí que quiere conservar ese título por el bien de mi hijo y el honor de mi familia", declaraba. “Sinceramente, pensé que Ilia sería la primera amenaza en el camino por ser considerado el más grande de todos los tiempos, y luego vimos lo que le pasó", analizaba Jon Jones en dicha entrevista. Sin embargo, pese a la derrota, la confianza de Jones en 'El Matador' se mantiene. “Pero cuando se trata de entretenimiento, su boxeo, su potencia, su confianza y todo lo demás... Me gusta cómo se comporta fuera de la jaula. Proviene de una familia exitosa y es un tipo que no necesita pelear, no necesita el dinero, pero lo hace por amor, y esas son las razones por las que me convertí en un gran admirador de Ilia”, decía... aunque el 'bulo' de la familia rica de Topuria está muy lejos de ser real. Solo cabe recordar cuando Topuria compaginaba varios trabajos en Alicante antes de dedicarse profesionalmente a las MMA. Ambos, por cierto, comparten representación en First Round Management.

articles.title: Alex Pereira Makes Surprising U-Turn on Herb Dean After Public Criticism
articles.summary: After publicly blasting Herb Dean for months, Alex Pereira admits he feels a bit sad for the veteran official amidst further backlash from fans.
articles.body:
Alex Pereira's feud with Herb Dean became one of the biggest talking points after UFC Freedom 250. The Brazilian was chasing history in the June 14 co-main event, hoping to become the first fighter in UFC history to win titles across three weight classes. However, those dreams came crashing down when Ciryl Gane stopped him in the second round.

The finish quickly became a source of debate, with fans questioning whether Gane's 11-strike sequence, including six blows to the back of Pereira's head, played a role in the stoppage. Pereira was particularly unhappy with Dean's handling of the exchange and publicly called out the veteran referee for failing to step in.

'Poatan' even urged the UFC to make sure Dean would no longer officiate his fights . The referee faced further scrutiny for his controversial handling of the Shara Magomedov vs. Michel Pereira fight at UFC Baku.

Dana White also acknowledged that Dean had endured a difficult year following the controversial first-round stoppage in the King Green vs. Esteban Ribovics fight at UFC 332. While Pereira's criticism made it seem like the feud was far from over, the Brazilian has now taken a surprisingly different stance and shown some sympathy for the veteran official.

Alex Pereira Feels Bad for Herb Dean but Still Doesn't Want Him Refereeing His Fights

Since the White House event, Dean has faced plenty of backlash from fans, even getting booed at events. The criticism has continued since June 2026, and it seems Pereira is starting to feel a little sympathy for the veteran referee.

In a recent interview with Ariel Helwani , the Brazilian opened up about the situation and explained why he initially called Dean out. Speaking in Portuguese, Pereira said, "I see everything that's going on, and sometimes I do feel bad because I know it's his job, but when I spoke, I was just advocating because he's the guy to be there who's supposed to be protecting the fighters and avoid that something worse could happen to a fighter."

He also admitted that while he stands by what he said, seeing the backlash against Dean hasn't been easy. Pereira added, "I had to speak my mind. But yeah, I do feel bad for him sometimes, some certain ways."

However, feeling sympathy for Dean hasn't changed Pereira's stance on having him officiate his fights. The former two-division champion still wants to keep the referee away from his future bouts. He said, "I don't know how things role in the fight night, but if I can have a choice, I definitely don't want him refereeing my fights no more."

Pereira is now preparing for a five-round co-main event against Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 on December 12. The matchup could have major implications for the heavyweight title picture, making the officiating an interesting subplot to watch. It remains to be seen whether Dean will be assigned to Pereira's fight or whether the Brazilian will have to deal with another referee.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Your questions answered ahead of Tyson Fury's Principality Stadium showdown with Anthony Joshua
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have had a rivalry for almost 10 years; Ahead of their December 11 showdown at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Sky Sports boxing experts Andy Scott and John Dennen answer readers' questions on a bonus episode of the Toe2Toe podcast
articles.body:
Of their shared opponents, who do you think did the best? (Craig)

They've both fought Oleksandr Usyk twice and they've both lost to him twice. Joshua did not box well in his first one but put in a stronger performance second time around. Fury though was impressive in his first Usyk fight, he looked strong in the first half of that first fight. At that level, with that opponent, Fury did do the best.

But they've both fought Francis Ngannou and Fury struggled whereas Joshua levelled the former UFC champion.

Both have boxed Wladimir Klitschko, Joshua did so later than Fury. AJ faced an older Klitschko, but perhaps one who'd learned lessons from his Fury fight. Klitschko though did give Joshua a more torrid fight while Fury exerted more control and won a decision in Germany. Ultimately Fury seems to come out ahead of Joshua against their highest level shared opponents, but hard to call really.

What does the future hold for each fighter if they win or lose? Will they seek a trilogy with Usyk? (Nem)

Fury will seek it, but whether there's a market for it is another question. Daniel Dubois could be an easier sell for the winner.

Neither Fury nor Joshua have a win over Usyk. Their first fights were intriguing enough to justify their rematches. But a trilogy with Usyk for either Fury or Joshua probably isn't needed.

Why is there a championship belt up for grabs? (Several)

The WBA has decided to sanction this for a 'super' title. We don't know why, frankly, and the WBA hasn't explained its reasoning. Both are former champions but the WBA already had a 'regular' titlist in Murat Gassiev and neither Fury nor Joshua were rated as the WBA's No 1 contender going into the fight.

It's the battle of each other and it doesn't need any belt on the line.

This isn't happening without Turki Alalshikh, the chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority. The press release to announce the fight did say he's doing it in partnership with Dana White, which opens the Pandora's Box of what can Dana White's involvement be alongside the contract that Eddie Hearn and Anthony Joshua have and what contract Frank Warren and Tyson Fury have. But Turki Alalshikh is putting up the money, he is the promoter of the event.

Obviously a huge fight, albeit later than hoped. Given there have been losses on either side, who do you think needs the win the most, based on skills, class, character, history and fan base? (Boon)

Anthony Joshua does have an outstanding resume and has fought high-quality opponents. But he hasn't fought Deontay Wilder, who Fury's boxed three times. Fury, albeit at different times, has held every major heavyweight world title and over the course of two Usyk fights arguably performed better.

For his legacy, Anthony Joshua probably does need the win more. A great question though that you can argue either way.

Just wondering how both fighters can adjust their bodies/minds to be able to fight in the early hours of the morning in the UK, just for the US audience to be able to watch the fight? (Peter)

A lot of the fights we've covered in Saudi Arabia for example were taking place in the early hours of the morning there. Joseph Parker when we visited him in camp was not getting up until 4.30pm, was then having his breakfast at 5pm and working out at 2am. These guys will move everything and settle into a schedule and a rhythm. Fury is already on US time, training in America.

For the US audience, although it's two Brits in the fight, the massive Netflix audience is coast to coast in America and they will expect to get better viewing figures at that time.

Will the loser of the fight retire? (Raz)

It depends on the manner of defeat. Fury's been vocal that he wants to go on as long as he can, but he has retired and unretired several times before. He could do that again.

For Anthony Joshua, a heavy loss might well force him to contemplate retirement. And if he does consider hanging up the gloves after this fight, as an Olympic gold medallist, as a two-time unified world heavyweight champion and British boxing superstar, Joshua has nothing left to prove.

Do you think Joshua will have the engine to keep up with Fury if it goes 12 rounds? (Sean)

Joshua's been 12 rounds on five different occasions. There's been no suggestion that he has any issues with his stamina. He is more musclebound and Fury has a natural rhythm but Fury doesn't set a relentless pace. Fury would have to make Joshua think and fight at a pace he's not used to and make him work harder than he normally would.

What would happen after 12 rounds if the decision was a draw? Do we get a rematch? (Richard)

A rematch in that scenario would be almost inevitable. If it's a draw they'd have to go again. They'd have learned lots about each other, it could be hyped all over again. They'd have to run it back.

We know AJ can be knocked down/out but do you think Fury has the power to put AJ down? (Paul)

In years gone by Fury wasn't deemed to punch his full weight. But he changed those assumptions with his devastating performances in the second and third fights with Deontay Wilder. Joshua has been hurt too, most recently and most worryingly by Kristian Prenga. Fury is certainly dangerous for him.

Why didn't they host this fight in Wembley? (Nas)

It doesn't have a roof. The weather at that time of year is probably more of a factor than licensing the late main event start time.

Who is going to be on the undercard in Cardiff? Will there be any Welsh boxers on it? (Jase)

We don't know yet. Dana White is looking to make Jai Opetaia versus Deontay Wilder on that bill. Queensberry will have a fighter on the undercard, so will Matchroom. We await confirmation of the card and it would be great to see Welsh boxers showcased on that bill. We will have to wait and see though.

For more questions and answers, including whether the fight will go the distance and how different it could have been eight years ago, listen to the full special edition of the Toe2Toe podcast here

articles.standfirst: La velada del 31 de octubre en Riad que encabezan Canelo Álvarez y Christian Mbilli sigue adelante, pero la tensión en Oriente Medio inquieta a algunos de los protagonistas
articles.summary: La velada del 31 de octubre en Riad que encabezan Canelo Álvarez y Christian Mbilli sigue adelante, pero la tensión en Oriente Medio inquieta a algunos de los protagonistas
articles.body: La inestabilidad persiste y la tensión sigue creciendo en Oriente Medio, y es que las misiones diplomáticas estadounidenses de toda la región emitieron el pasado domingo una nueva ronda de advertencias de seguridad dirigidas a sus ciudadanos ante la escalada de ataques de las milicias hutíes de Yemen contra Arabia Saudí. Recordemos que el pasado 10 de octubre 13 personas murieron y más de 300 resultaron heridas en un ataque contra el aeropuerto internacional Rey Khalid de Riad. Sin ir más lejos, hoy se ha reportado el fallecimiento de una persona en un ataque al aeropuerto internacional Rey Fahd de Dammam, en el este de Arabía Saudí. Las alertas, emitidas el domingo por las embajadas estadounidenses en Arabia Saudita, Baréin, Catar, los Emiratos Árabes Unidos y otros países, advertían que las hostilidades podrían extenderse rápidamente y sin previo aviso más allá de las zonas ya afectadas por los combates. Los avisos instaban a los estadounidenses a mantenerse alerta y prepararse para posibles cancelaciones de vuelos, cierres del espacio aéreo y otras interrupciones en los viajes. Es decir, el riesgo existe y quien esté en dichas zonas o esté pensando en desplazarse hacia allí debe estar preparado para cualquier escenario. Obviamente, el deporte no es ajeno a esto y hay importantes eventos programados por parte de Arabia Saudí en su territorio próximamente. La semana pasada asistimos a la cancelación del Mundial de Ciclismo Urbano y el Six Kings Slam de tenis, que debía estar jugándose ya, se pospuso a finales de diciembre; el Rally Dakar no está garantizado y ahora el foco se ha desplazado a la velada de boxeo que encabezarán Saúl ‘Canelo’ Álvarez y Christian Mbilli en Riad el 31 de octubre. De lo que suceda con este evento estará también muy pendiente WWE, que el 7 de noviembre celebra 'Crown Jewel: Riyadh'. Hace unos días el conocido promotor de boxeo Turki Alalshikh, que a su vez es presidente de la Autoridad General de Entretenimiento de Arabia Saudí y tiene rango de ministro, trató de calmar a quienes dudaban de que la velada tendrá lugar, a través de un mensaje en redes que decía: “Canelo se comunicó conmigo y me dijo que todavía peleará en Riad este octubre, pase lo que pase. No le teme a nada”. En principio todo sigue adelante en el evento denominado ‘México contra el mundo’, pero en la misma cartelera ya hay equipos que dudan de que la misma se pueda realizar en Riad ahora. El primero en levantar la mano ha sido el afamado entrenador Robert García, quien acudirá a la capital saudita con su boxeador Lindolfo Delgado para medirse a Arthur Biyarslanov por el título mundial vacante de peso superligero de la IBF. El caso es que García quería que su peleador se desplazara al menos siete días antes de la pelea a Riad, pero todavía no le han mandado los billetes. “Mi equipo, al menos el equipo con Lindolfo Delgado, estuvimos esperando todo el fin de semana pasado esperando. No tenemos vuelos, no tenemos información, así que, sinceramente, no sé qué va a pasar”, expresó a BoxingScene. El preparador californiano, insistió: “No podemos quedarnos sentados, esperando y pensando: ‘Aquí estamos esperando ese vuelo. Nos lo enviarán’. Ya deberían haberlo hecho”. Está claro que existe incertidumbre, pero García fue un poco más allá al afirmar: “No quiero aparecer en un documental dentro de 25 años hablando de todos esos valientes luchadores, entrenadores y directivos que fueron allí [a Arabia Saudí] y nunca regresaron”. Sin duda el entrenador mostró su preocupación más allá de si recibe los billetes de avión o no.

articles.body:
ABU DHABI – The UFC 333 pre-fight press conference takes place Thursday, and you can watch a live stream of the event in the video above. The press conference takes place at Etihad Arena, which also hosts Saturday's fight card.

UFC 333 is built around two championship fights: A featherweight title main event of Alexander Volkanovski (28-4 MMA, 15-3 UFC) vs. Movsar Evloev (20-0 MMA, 10-0 UFC) and a bantamweight title trilogy co-headliner of Petr Yan (20-5 MMA, 12-4 UFC) vs. Merab Dvalishvili (21-3 MMA, 14-3 UFC).

Here's what you need to know about the UFC 333 press conference.

What time does the UFC 333 press conference start?

The UFC 333 press conference starts at 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT, which is 5 p.m. local time in Abu Dhabi.

Who's taking part in the UFC 333 press conference?

Four fighters from the two championship bouts are slated to participate in the UFC 333 press conference: Volkanovski, Evloev, Yan and Dvalishvili.

UFC CEO Dana White will oversee the UFC 333 pre-fight press conference.
